On the kernel rows the interesting allocation is the stack's Object[].\n247\t    private val ProfLine = \"\"\"(?m)^.*?(\\d+)\\s+[\\d.]+%\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\S.*?)\\s*$\"\"\".r\n248\t\n249\t    def parseAlloc(raw: String): Chunk[AllocSite] =\n250\t        Chunk.from(ProfLine.findAllMatchIn(raw).map(m => AllocSite(m.group(3), m.group(1).toLong, m.group(2).toLong)).toSeq)\n251\t\n252\t    def parseCpu(raw: String): Chunk[CpuSite] =\n253\t        Chunk.from(ProfLine.findAllMatchIn(raw).map(m => CpuSite(m.group(3), m.group(1).toLong)).toSeq)\n254\t\n255\t    /** The collapsed (FlameGraph folded) allocation view: `frame;frame;...;Class_[i] value`.\n256\t      *\n257\t      * Three things about this format decide whether a parse of it means anything, and all three were\n258\t      * got wrong in the first design of this phase:\n259\t      *\n260\t      *   - **It is root-first.** `frames.head` is `java.lang.Thread.run` on every line. The allocated\n261\t      *     class is the *last* frame and the method that allocated it is the one before that, so both\n262\t      *     are indexed from the leaf end.\n263\t      *   - **The value is a sample count**, because the dump JMH issues carries no `total` option.\n264\t      *     Comparing it against the flat table's bytes is comparing two different quantities, and a\n265\t      *     conservation gate written that way can never pass.\n266\t      *   - **The leaf carries a TLAB marker**, `_[i]` inside and `_[k]` outside, which is part of the\n267\t      *     sample and not part of the class name.\n268\t      */\n269\t    def parseCollapsed(raw: String): Chunk[AllocByMethod] =\n270\t        val entries =\n271\t            raw.linesIterator.flatMap { line =>\n272\t                val cut = line.lastIndexOf(' ')\n273\t                if cut <= 0 then None\n274\t                else\n275\t                    val (stack, value) = (line.substring(0, cut), line.substring(cut + 1).trim)\n276\t                    value.toLongOption.flatMap { n =>\n277\t                        val frames = stack.split(';').filter(_.nonEmpty).map(_.replace('/', '.'))\n278\t                        if frames.length < 2 then None\n279\t                        else\n280\t                            val cls    = frames.last.replaceAll(\"_\\\\[[a-z]\\\\]$\", \"\")\n281\t                            val method = frames(frames.length - 2)\n282\t                            // walk out past the type's own frames. Every Nested on the nested-payload\n283\t                            // row is minted at `Nested$.apply`, which decides nothing; one frame\n284\t                            // further out is who asked for it.\n285\t                            val own  = Seq(cls + \".\", cls + \"$.\")\n286\t                            val site = frames.init.reverseIterator.find(f => !own.exists(f.startsWith)).getOrElse(method)\n287\t                            Some(((cls, method, site), n))\n288\t                    }\n289\t            }.toSeq\n290\t        Chunk.from(\n291\t            entries.groupMapReduce(_._1)(_._2)(_ + _).toSeq\n292\t                .map((k, n) => AllocByMethod(k._1, k._2, n, Maybe.empty, k._3))\n293\t                .sortBy(-_.samples)\n294\t        )\n295\t    end parseCollapsed\n296\t\n297\t    /** Turns the collapsed sample counts into byte estimates using the flat table's bytes per class.\n298\t      *\n299\t      * Only ever an apportionment: the profiler weights each sample by the bytes it stands for, and\n300\t      * that weighting is not recoverable per frame from a sample count. Within one class the sizes\n301\t      * are near-constant, which is what makes the split usable, and it is labelled an estimate.\n302\t      */\n303\t    def apportion(flat: Chunk[AllocSite], byMethod: Chunk[AllocByMethod]): Chunk[AllocByMethod] =\n304\t        val perClass = flat.map(a => a.cls -> a).toMap\n305\t        val totals   = byMethod.groupMapReduce(_.cls)(_.samples)(_ + _)\n306\t        byMethod.map { m =>\n307\t            val estimate =\n308\t                for\n309\t                    site  <- Maybe.fromOption(perClass.get(m.cls))\n310\t                    total <- Maybe.fromOption(totals.get(m.cls)).filter(_ > 0)\n311\t                yield site.bytes.toDouble * m.samples / total\n312\t            m.copy(bytes = estimate)\n313\t        }\n314\t    end apportion\n315\t\n316\t    /** Whether the two views describe the same samples, per class.\n317\t      *\n318\t      * A coverage guard and nothing more: it holds equally for a correct attribution and for one that\n319\t      * assigns every sample of a class to a single arbitrary frame. What it does catch is the parse\n320\t      * losing lines, which is the failure this file has had four times. Both views must come from one\n321\t      * recording, or the comparison is bounded by run-to-run variance instead of by parser\n322\t      * correctness: two recordings of the same planted program differed by 0.25% on the same class.\n323\t      */\n324\t    def allocConservation(flat: Chunk[AllocSite], byMethod: Chunk[AllocByMethod]): Chunk[String] =\n325\t        val totals = byMethod.groupMapReduce(_.cls)(_.samples)(_ + _)\n326\t        flat.filter(_.samples > 0).flatMap { site =>\n327\t            val got = totals.getOrElse(site.cls, 0L)\n328\t            if got == site.samples then Chunk.empty\n329\t            else Chunk(s\"${site.cls}: flat table has ${site.samples} samples, the collapsed view accounts for $got\")\n330\t        }\n331\t    end allocConservation\n332\t\n333\t    // --- one leg ----------------------------------------------------------------\n334\t\n335\t    def openSession(worktree: Path, driftRow: String)(using Frame): Session < (Async & Fail) =\n336\t        for\n337\t            _    <- requireThrowaway(worktree)\n338\t            // start from a defined tree: a previous bracket leaves its last leg's sources in place\n339\t            _    <- resetWorktree(worktree, Cli.protoPaths)\n340\t            _    <- requireClean(worktree)\n341\t            host <- exec(worktree, \"hostname\").map(_.trim)\n342\t            jvm  <- System.property[String](\"java.version\", \"unknown\")\n343\t            now  <- Clock.now\n344\t        // no drift measurement here any more. A bracket estimates its spread from its own replicate\n345\t        // legs, which is both a better estimate and one taken on the same tree as the measurement;\n346\t        // the old session drift was three extra runs on HEAD sources belonging to neither leg, and\n347\t        // keeping both left two competing noise estimates with the report using the worse one.\n348\t        yield Session(s\"s-${now.toDuration.toMillis}\", host, jvm, 0.0)\n349\t\n350\t    def runLeg(\n351\t        session: Session,\n352\t        worktree: Path,\n353\t        label: String,\n354\t        sha: String,\n355\t        paths: Seq[String],\n356\t        markerSpecs: Seq[(String, String, String)],\n357\t        rows: Seq[String],\n358\t        forks: Int,\n359\t        evidence: Evidence,\n360\t        /** Extra JVM arguments for this leg. Without these a configuration probe is inexpressible and\n361\t          * every falsifier that is a JVM flag has to be run by hand, which is how the two experiments\n362\t          * that diagnosed a live regression were actually run: by a shell script the harness knew\n363\t          * nothing about.\n364\t          */\n365\t        jvmArgs: Seq[String] = Nil,\n366\t        attempts: Int = 3\n367\t    )(using Frame): Run < (Async & Fail) =\n368\t        val selector   = if rows.isEmpty then s\"$BenchClass.*\" else rows.map(r => s\"$BenchClass.$r\").mkString(\" \")\n369\t        val wholeClass = rows.isEmpty\n370\t        val json       = worktree / s\"bench-$label.json\"\n371\t\n372\t        def sbt(task: String) = exec(worktree, \"sbt\", \"--client\", task).map { out =>\n373\t            // A JVM that cannot parse a compile command prints one line and runs anyway, producing a\n374\t            // measurement that looks entirely normal and tests nothing. Two runs were spent that way\n375\t            // before a log line revealed `CompileCommand: An error occurred during parsing`, and both\n376\t            // had already been read as results.\n377\t            if rejectedCompileCommand(out).nonEmpty then\n378\t                Abort.fail(BracketFailed(\n379\t                    \"the JVM rejected a compile command and ran anyway; the measurement tests nothing. \" +\n380\t                        \"Use -XX:CompileCommandFile, which does not have to survive shell and sbt quoting:\\n\" +\n381\t                        rejectedCompileCommand(out).take(3).mkString(\"\\n\")\n382\t                ))\n383\t            else out\n384\t        }\n385\t\n386\t        // pinned on every leg: these rows allocate megabytes per operation, so ergonomic\n387\t        // heap sizing is a live variance source that costs one flag to remove\n388\t        val extraVm = (Seq(\"-Xms4g\", \"-Xmx4g\", \"-XX:+UseG1GC\") ++ jvmArgs).mkString(\" \")\n389\t\n390\t        def measureWith(warmup: Int, n: Int, expected: Int): Chunk[Row] < (Async & Fail) =\n391\t            // the results file is deleted first, every attempt. It is a fixed path per label, so a\n392\t            // run that matched no benchmarks (which JMH exits 0 for, and which is the exact failure\n393\t            // the retry below exists for) would otherwise leave the *previous* attempt's json in\n394\t            // place, and this leg would silently adopt the previous leg's numbers with a row count\n395\t            // that passes every check.\n396\t            json.removeExisting\n397\t                .andThen(sbt(\n398\t                    s\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f $forks -wi $warmup -i $MeasureIterations -r ${IterationSeconds}s \" +\n399\t                        s\"-w ${IterationSeconds}s -prof gc -prof comp -rf json -rff ${json.toString} \" +\n400\t                        \"-jvmArgsAppend \\\"\" + extraVm + \"\\\" \" + selector\n401\t                ))\n402\t                .andThen(json.exists)\n403\t                .map { wrote =>\n404\t                    Abort.when(!wrote)(BracketFailed(\n405\t                        s\"leg $label produced no results file at $json. JMH exits 0 when its selector matches \" +\n406\t                            \"nothing, so this is a run that measured no benchmark rather than a run that failed.\"\n407\t                    ))\n408\t                }\n409\t                .andThen(json.read)\n410\t                .map(parseJmh)\n411\t                .map { parsed =>\n412\t                    val want = if wholeClass then expected else rows.size\n413\t                    if parsed.size == want then parsed\n414\t                    // the first invocation after a recompile can match nothing; a short read is a\n415\t                    // failed run, never a clean one\n416\t                    else if n < attempts then measureWith(warmup, n + 1, expected)\n417\t                    else Abort.fail(BracketFailed(s\"leg $label produced ${parsed.size}/$want rows after $attempts attempts\"))\n418\t                }\n419\t\n420\t        // both views of the allocation profile come out of one recording, which is the only way the\n421\t        // conservation check between them measures the parse rather than run-to-run variance: JMH\n422\t        // stops the profiler once and dumps it twice. `text` is printed inline and carries the bytes;\n423\t        // `collapsed` is written to a file and carries the stacks.\n424\t        val allocDir = worktree / s\"alloc-$label\"\n425\t\n426\t        def profile(event: String, extra: String = \"\") =\n427\t            sbt(\n428\t                s\"\"\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f 1 -wi $WarmupIterations -i 1 -r ${IterationSeconds}s -w ${IterationSeconds}s \"\"\" +\n429\t                    s\"\"\"-prof \"async:libPath=$AsyncProf;event=$event$extra\" $selector\"\"\"\n430\t            )\n431\t\n432\t        /** The collapsed dumps JMH leaves on disk, wherever under `dir` it decided to put them. */\n433\t        def collapsedFiles(using Frame): Chunk[Path] < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException]) =\n434\t            allocDir.exists.map {\n435\t                case false => Chunk.empty[Path]: Chunk[Path] < Any\n436\t                case true =>\n437\t                    allocDir.list.map { entries =>\n438\t                        Kyo.foreach(entries) { e =>\n439\t                            e.list.map(_.filter(_.name.exists(n => n.startsWith(\"collapsed\") && n.endsWith(\".csv\"))))\n440\t                                .handle(Abort.recover[FileFsException](_ => Chunk.empty[Path]))\n441\t                        }.map(_.flatten)\n442\t                    }\n443\t            }\n444\t\n445\t        val logcFile = worktree / s\"logc-$label.xml\"\n446\t\n447\t        /** The only source of inlining decisions.\n448\t          *\n449\t          * The `PrintInlining` run this replaces cost a whole JMH invocation to produce strictly less: no denominator per method, no\n450\t          * deoptimizations, no receiver profiles, and output interleaved across compiler threads so its tree could not be trusted. One run\n451\t          * removed from every leg.\n452\t          */\n453\t        def compilationLog =\n454\t            sbt(\n455\t                s\"\"\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f 1 -wi $WarmupIterations -i 1 -jvmArgsAppend \"-XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions -XX:+LogCompilation -XX:LogFile=${logcFile.toString}\" $selector\"\"\"\n456\t            ).andThen(logcFile.read).map(LogCompilation.parse)\n457\t\n458\t        for\n459\t            _        <- requireThrowaway(worktree)\n460\t            _        <- restore(worktree, sha, paths)\n461\t            declared <- declaredRows(worktree)\n462\t            // a faster variant whose suite is red is not a result; gate before spending the runs.\n463\t            // this also settles the sources: the build formats on compile, so the baseline below\n464\t            // must be taken after it or the leg invalidates itself on its own formatting\n465\t            _          <- requireGreenSuite(worktree, \"kyo-kernel2JVM/testOnly kyo.kernel.proto.*\")\n466\t            before     <- readMarkers(worktree, markerSpecs)\n467\t            hashBefore <- treeHash(worktree, paths)\n468\t            measured   <- measureWith(WarmupIterations, 1, declared)\n469\t            allocOut <- if evidence == Evidence.Full then profile(\"alloc\", s\";output=text,collapsed;dir=${allocDir.toString}\")\n470\t            else \"\": String < Any\n471\t            allocSites = parseAlloc(allocOut)\n472\t            collapsed <- collapsedFiles.map(fs => Kyo.foreach(fs)(_.read)).map(_.mkString(\"\\n\"))\n473\t            byMethod   = apportion(allocSites, parseCollapsed(collapsed))\n474\t            // the collapsed dump is requested by an option string that has to survive shell, sbt and\n475\t            // JMH quoting. When it does not, JMH runs the profiler anyway and prints a normal-looking\n476\t            // table, so the leg would report allocation with no attribution and nothing would say the\n477\t            // instruction had been dropped. A rejected compile command taught this exact lesson twice.\n478\t            _ <- Abort.when(evidence == Evidence.Full && allocSites.nonEmpty && byMethod.isEmpty)(\n479\t                BracketFailed(\n480\t                    s\"leg $label profiled ${allocSites.size} allocated classes but produced no collapsed view, \" +\n481\t                        s\"so nothing can be attributed to a method. Expected a collapsed-*.csv under $allocDir; \" +\n482\t                        \"check that output=text,collapsed reached JMH.\"\n483\t                )\n484\t            )\n485\t            cpuSites  <- if evidence == Evidence.Full then profile(\"itimer\").map(parseCpu) else Chunk.empty[CpuSite]: Chunk[CpuSite] < Any\n486\t            logc       <- if evidence == Evidence.Full then compilationLog else LogCompilation.Parsed(Chunk.empty, Chunk.empty, 0, Chunk.empty): LogCompilation.Parsed < Any\n487\t            after      <- readMarkers(worktree, markerSpecs)\n488\t            _          <- Abort.when(before != after)(BracketFailed(s\"leg $label markers moved mid-run: $before -> $after\"))\n489\t            hashAfter  <- treeHash(worktree, paths)\n490\t            // sources must not be edited while a run is in flight; if they were, the numbers describe no single tree\n491\t            _   <- Abort.when(hashBefore != hashAfter)(BracketFailed(s\"leg $label sources changed mid-run\"))\n492\t            now <- Clock.now\n493\t        yield Run(\n494\t            id = s\"$label-${sha.take(10)}-${now.toDuration.toMillis}\",\n495\t            session = session,\n496\t            treeHash = hashAfter,\n497\t            label = label,\n498\t            sha = sha,\n499\t            forks = forks,\n500\t            evidence = evidence,\n501\t            wholeClass = wholeClass,\n502\t            declaredRows = declared,\n503\t            markers = before,\n504\t            warmup = WarmupIterations,\n505\t            rows = measured,\n506\t            jit = LogCompilation.inlining(logc),\n507\t            coverage = logc.coverage,\n508\t            jvmArgs = Chunk.from(jvmArgs),\n509\t            alloc = allocSites,\n510\t            allocByMethod = byMethod,\n511\t            cpu = cpuSites,\n512\t            jit_metrics =\n513\t                if evidence == Evidence.Full then\n514\t                    Maybe(LogCompilation.metrics(\n515\t                        logc,\n516\t                        measured.flatMap(_.compilerMsProfiled).sum,\n517\t                        measured.flatMap(_.compilerMsTotal).sum\n518\t                    ))\n519\t                else Maybe.empty,\n520\t            deopts = LogCompilation.deoptSummary(logc),\n521\t            morphism = LogCompilation.morphism(logc),\n522\t            recordedAt = now.show\n523\t        )\n524\t        end for\n525\t    end runLeg\n526\t\n527\t    // --- comparison (pure, over stored runs) ------------------------------------\n528\t\n529\t    def band(control: Run, variant: Run): Double =\n530\t        val measured = Math.max(control.session.driftPercent, variant.session.driftPercent)\n531\t        if measured > 0.0 then measured else DriftBand\n532\t\n533\t    /** Fraction of a run's sampled time in classes no kernel change can move. */\n534\t    def noiseShare(run: Run): Double =\n535\t        val total = run.cpu.map(_.nanos).sum\n536\t        if total == 0L then 0.0\n537\t        else run.cpu.filter(c => KnownNoise.exists(c.method.contains)).map(_.nanos).sum.toDouble / total * 100\n538\t\n539\t    /** Rows whose measured window still contained meaningful compilation.\n540\t      *\n541\t      * Deliberately not corrected by warming longer. A benchmark that needs unusual warmup is reporting something about the code under it,\n542\t      * bigger methods, recompilation churn, or an unstable profile, and warming past it discards the finding. The flag exists so the cause\n543\t      * gets diagnosed.\n544\t      */\n545\t    def stillCompiling(run: Run): Chunk[(String, Double)] =\n546\t        val measuredMs = run.forks * MeasureIterations * IterationSeconds * 1000.0\n547\t        Chunk.from(run.rows.flatMap { r =>\n548\t            r.compilingShare(measuredMs).filter(_ > CompilingShareLimit).map(share => r.name -> share)\n549\t        })\n550\t\n551\t    def sameSession(control: Run, variant: Run): Boolean =\n552\t        control.session.id == variant.session.id\n553\t\n554\t    def compare(control: Run, variant: Run): Comparison =\n555\t        val deltas = Chunk.from(control.rows).flatMap { c =>\n556\t            Chunk.from(variant.row(c.name)).map { v =>\n557\t                val percent = (v.score - c.score) / c.score * 100\n558\t                // never tighter than either leg's own uncertainty. The drift band alone classified a\n559\t                // -9.8% delta as a win on a row whose control leg reported +-15.2%, which is the same\n560\t                // defect the replicate statistic had and had already been fixed there: a threshold\n561\t                // below the measurement's own error classifies that error as a result.\n562\t                val ownError = Math.max(c.relativeError, v.relativeError) * 100\n563\t                val drift    = Math.max(band(control, variant), ownError)\n564\t                val verdict =\n565\t                    // a score whose error is a large fraction of itself cannot support a percentage\n566\t                    if c.error > c.score * 0.5 || c.score <= 0.0 then Verdict.BelowResolution\n567\t                    else if percent < -drift then Verdict.Faster\n568\t                    else if percent > drift then Verdict.Regressed\n569\t                    else Verdict.Flat\n570\t                val allocDelta =\n571\t                    for\n572\t                        ca <- c.allocPerOp\n573\t                        va <- v.allocPerOp\n574\t                    yield va - ca\n575\t                // a row inside the band has not moved, so nothing explains it. Both stored e2e runs\n576\t                // printed a mechanism beside +0.8% and +0.3% deltas, which invites the reader to\n577\t                // believe a cause was found for a difference that is not there.\n578\t                val mechanism =\n579\t                    if verdict == Verdict.Flat || verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution then Chunk.empty\n580\t                    else\n581\t                        Chunk.from(Seq(\n582\t                            allocDelta.filter(d => Math.abs(d) > 1.0).map(d => f\"allocation ${d}%+.0f B/op\"),\n583\t                            jitShift(control, variant).headMaybe.map(m => s\"inlining changed: $m\")\n584\t                        ).flatMap(_.toOption))\n585\t                // a single pair cannot support a t threshold, but it can state the floor it used,\n586\t                // so a flat row is bounded rather than merely quiet\n587\t                Delta(c.name, c, v, percent, verdict, allocDelta, mechanism, Maybe(Resolution(drift, drift * c.score / 100, 0, 0.0)))\n588\t            }\n589\t        }.sortBy(d => (d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution, d.percent))\n590\t        Comparison(control, variant, deltas, jitShift(control, variant))\n591\t    end compare\n592\t\n593\t    /** Family-wise error rate a session is willing to accept across all its rows. */\n594\t    val FamilyAlpha = 0.05\n595\t\n596\t    /** Which design each leg of a bracket measures, in order.\n597\t      *\n598\t      * Control, variant, control, variant, control. Interleaved because measuring all the controls\n599\t      * first and all the variants second confounds the design with everything that drifts over the\n600\t      * session: the variant would always run on a hotter machine, and that bias points the same way\n601\t      * every time. Replicated because a threshold needs a spread estimated from more than one pair,\n602\t      * and three controls against two variants gives three degrees of freedom.\n603\t      *\n604\t      * Pure and separately testable: the ordering is the part worth checking, and checking it should\n605\t      * not cost a half-hour run.\n606\t      */\n607\t    /** One arm of a bracket: the sources it measures and the JVM configuration it measures them under.\n608\t      *\n609\t      * Both, because a comparison is not always between two designs. The campaign's central question,\n610\t      * whether forcing one method to inline recovers a regression, is one design under two JVM\n611\t      * configurations, and a bracket that could only flip shas could not express it. Every such\n612\t      * comparison was therefore run as a single unreplicated leg, which is why they all report a floor\n613\t      * rather than a threshold.\n614\t      */\n615\t    case class Arm(sha: String, jvmArgs: Seq[String] = Nil)\n616\t\n617\t    /** The C V C V C ordering, alternating so machine drift lands in both arms rather than one.\n618\t      *\n619\t      * Generic in what a leg measures because `bracket` compares two `Arm`s and the test that pins\n620\t      * this ordering compares two shas. It was written twice for that reason, once here and once\n621\t      * inline in `bracket`, so the test covered a function the runner did not call and the ordering\n622\t      * that actually ran was pinned by nothing.\n623\t      */\n624\t    def bracketPlan[A](control: A, variant: A, legs: Int = 5): Chunk[(String, A)] =\n625\t        Chunk.from(\n626\t            (0 until Math.max(2, legs)).map { i =>\n627\t                if i % 2 == 0 then (s\"control-${i / 2 + 1}\", control)\n628\t                else (s\"variant-${i / 2 + 1}\", variant)\n629\t            }\n630\t        )\n631\t\n632\t    /** One bracket: every leg of `bracketPlan`, measured in order, split into controls and variants.\n633\t      *\n634\t      * The legs are run through the same `runLeg` as a single measurement, so every guard applies to\n635\t      * each of them: the suite must be green, markers must not move, sources must not change mid-run.\n636\t      */\n637\t    def bracket(\n638\t        session: Session,\n639\t        worktree: Path,\n640\t        control: Arm,\n641\t        variant: Arm,\n642\t        paths: Seq[String],\n643\t        markerSpecs: Seq[(String, String, String)],\n644\t        rows: Seq[String],\n645\t        forks: Int,\n646\t        evidence: Evidence,\n647\t        legs: Int = 5\n648\t    )(using Frame): (Chunk[Run], Chunk[Run]) < (Async & Fail) =\n649\t        Kyo.foreach(bracketPlan(control, variant, legs)) { (label, arm) =>\n650\t            runLeg(session, worktree, label, arm.sha, paths, markerSpecs, rows, forks, evidence, arm.jvmArgs)\n651\t        }.map { ls =>\n652\t            (Chunk.from(ls.filter(_.label.startsWith(\"control\"))), Chunk.from(ls.filter(_.label.startsWith(\"variant\"))))\n653\t        }\n654\t    end bracket\n655\t\n656\t    /** A chain of shas, each step isolating one change from the step before it.\n657\t      *\n658\t      * The reason this exists rather than a second pair: a two-sha comparison measures the difference\n659\t      * between two trees and cannot attribute it, because the partition between the changes inside\n660\t      * that diff was never declared. The skill's worked example is exactly this. Two changes shipped\n661\t      * together, a node-layout change and a currency hoist; the bundle was faster, the win was\n662\t      * credited first to one and then to the other, and both stories were wrong as told. Running the\n663\t      * pieces separately settled it, and running the pieces separately is a chain.\n664\t      *\n665\t      * Each adjacent pair is measured as its own replicated comparison, so every step carries a\n666\t      * threshold rather than a single difference of two numbers.\n667\t      */\n668\t    /** Why a proposed chain is not one, or empty when it is.\n669\t      *\n670\t      * Pure and separate from the runner so the refusal can be tested without a worktree: the whole\n671\t      * point of the guard is that it fires before a single leg is measured.\n672\t      */\n673\t    def requireChain(shas: Seq[String]): Maybe[String] =\n674\t        if shas.size < 3 then\n675\t            Maybe(\n676\t                s\"a chain needs three or more shas; ${shas.size} is a pair, and a pair cannot isolate anything. \" +\n677\t                    \"Use `bracket` for a pair, which reports that it attributes no source-level mechanism.\"\n678\t            )\n679\t        else if shas.distinct.size != shas.size then\n680\t            Maybe(s\"the chain repeats a sha (${shas.diff(shas.distinct).distinct.mkString(\", \")}); a step to the same tree isolates nothing\")\n681\t        else Maybe.empty\n682\t\n683\t    def chain(\n684\t        session: Session,\n685\t        worktree: Path,\n686\t        shas: Seq[String],\n687\t        paths: Seq[String],\n688\t        markerSpecs: Seq[(String, String, String)],\n689\t        rows: Seq[String],\n690\t        forks: Int,\n691\t        evidence: Evidence,\n692\t        legsPerSha: Int = 2\n693\t    )(using Frame): Chunk[(String, Chunk[Run])] < (Async & Fail) =\n694\t        requireChain(shas) match\n695\t        case Maybe.Present(why) => Abort.fail(BracketFailed(why))\n696\t        case _ =>\n697\t            // interleaved rather than grouped: measuring all of sha A then all of sha B puts any\n698\t            // machine drift entirely into the difference between them, which is the mistake the A/A\n699\t            // null's alternating split already exists to avoid\n700\t            val plan =\n701\t                Chunk.from(\n702\t                    (1 to Math.max(2, legsPerSha)).flatMap(rep => shas.zipWithIndex.map((sha, i) => (s\"s$i-$rep\", sha)))\n703\t                )\n704\t            Kyo.foreach(plan) { (label, sha) =>\n705\t                runLeg(session, worktree, label, sha, paths, markerSpecs, rows, forks, evidence)\n706\t            }.map { ls =>\n707\t                Chunk.from(shas.zipWithIndex.map((sha, i) => sha -> Chunk.from(ls.filter(_.label.startsWith(s\"s$i-\")))))\n708\t            }\n709\t    end chain\n710\t\n711\t    /** Compares replicate legs, which is the only shape that can support a threshold.\n712\t      *\n713\t      * A session measures control, variant, control, variant, control. Pooling the spread across those replicates is what makes a verdict\n714\t      * answerable for its own uncertainty; the single-pair `compare` above can classify against a drift band but cannot say how small an\n715\t      * effect it would have caught, so every flat row it produces is unbounded.\n716\t      */\n717\t    def compareReplicated(controls: Chunk[Run], variants: Chunk[Run]): Comparison =\n718\t        val rowNames = Chunk.from(controls.headMaybe.map(_.rows.map(_.name)).getOrElse(Chunk.empty))\n719\t        val reps =\n720\t            rowNames.map { name =>\n721\t                Stats.Replicated(\n722\t                    name,\n723\t                    Chunk.from(controls.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.score)),\n724\t                    Chunk.from(variants.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.score)),\n725\t                    // each leg's own relative error, so the threshold can never sit below it\n726\t                    Chunk.from((controls ++ variants).flatMap(_.row(name)).map(r => if r.score == 0.0 then 0.0 else r.error / r.score))\n727\t                )\n728\t            }\n729\t        val common = Stats.commonMode(reps)\n730\t        val deltas =\n731\t            reps.flatMap { r =>\n732\t                for\n733\t                    c0 <- Chunk.from(controls.headMaybe.flatMap(_.row(r.row)))\n734\t                    v0 <- Chunk.from(variants.headMaybe.flatMap(_.row(r.row)))\n735\t                yield\n736\t                    // the rows carried on the delta are the replicate MEANS, not the first leg's\n737\t                    // scores. Showing leg one beside a mean-based percentage let the table read\n738\t                    // \"6.17 -> 6.39 ... +0.0%\", where a reader computing the displayed numbers gets\n739\t                    // +3.6% and the harness is reporting something else entirely.\n740\t                    val c = c0.copy(score = r.controlMean, error = r.pooledSd.getOrElse(c0.error))\n741\t                    val v = v0.copy(score = r.variantMean, error = r.pooledSd.getOrElse(v0.error))\n742\t                    val (verdict, resolution) = Stats.classify(r, FamilyAlpha, rowNames.size)\n743\t                    val allocDelta =\n744\t                        for\n745\t                            ca <- c.allocPerOp\n746\t                            va <- v.allocPerOp\n747\t                        yield va - ca\n748\t                    val mechanism =\n749\t                        if verdict == Verdict.Flat || verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution then Chunk.empty\n750\t                        else\n751\t                            Chunk.from(Seq(\n752\t                                allocDelta.filter(d => Math.abs(d) > 1.0).map(d => f\"allocation ${d}%+.0f B/op\"),\n753\t                                jitShift(controls.head, variants.head).headMaybe.map(m => s\"inlining changed: $m\")\n754\t                            ).flatMap(_.toOption))\n755\t                    Delta(r.row, c, v, r.deltaPercent, verdict, allocDelta, mechanism, resolution)\n756\t            }.sortBy(d => (d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution, d.percent))\n757\t        Comparison(controls.head, variants.head, deltas, jitShift(controls.head, variants.head))\n758\t    end compareReplicated\n759\t\n760\t    /** The A/A null: control legs against each other, through the identical pipeline.\n761\t      *\n762\t      * Any row this classifies, and any mechanism it names, is false by construction. It is the only check here that can fail in the\n763\t      * direction that matters, since every other one asks the harness to stay silent and is therefore satisfied by silence.\n764\t      */\n765\t    def nullComparison(controls: Chunk[Run]): Maybe[Comparison] =\n766\t        // three control legs is the documented session (C V C V C), so requiring four made this\n767\t        // unreachable in the harness's own workflow: the one check that can fail in the direction\n768\t        // that matters never ran.\n769\t        if controls.size < 3 then Maybe.empty\n770\t        else\n771\t            // split by alternation, not by time. Contiguous halves group adjacent-in-time legs, which\n772\t            // understates leg-to-leg spread and puts any warm-up trend entirely in the numerator: over\n773\t            // six legs carrying a 3% monotone trend, contiguous halves report a regression of +1.79%\n774\t            // where alternating halves correctly report flat. The real comparison interleaves control\n775\t            // and variant legs, so the null has to interleave too or it is not measuring the same thing.\n776\t            val indexed = controls.zipWithIndex\n777\t            val a       = Chunk.from(indexed.filter((_, i) => i % 2 == 0).map((r, _) => r))\n778\t            val b       = Chunk.from(indexed.filter((_, i) => i % 2 == 1).map((r, _) => r))\n779\t            if a.isEmpty || b.isEmpty then Maybe.empty else Maybe(compareReplicated(a, b))\n780\t\n781\t    /** Methods whose inlining verdict moved decisively between the two runs.\n782\t      *\n783\t      * Decisive means unanimous on both sides: every site inlined in one leg and every site refused in the other. Anything less is a\n784\t      * fraction that moved, and those move on their own. In a captured pair, 11 of 85 kyo methods carried both verdicts, and for two of them\n785\t      * a single site out of six decided the method's reported verdict. Two runs of one identical comparison named disjoint \"mechanisms\" that\n786\t      * way, one of them a 2-byte method \"refused\" for size. Only a byte count moving with a unanimous flip can be a mechanism, so only that\n787\t      * is reported as one.\n788\t      */\n789\t    def jitShift(control: Run, variant: Run): Chunk[String] =\n790\t        Chunk.from(variant.jit.filter(_.method.startsWith(\"kyo.\"))).flatMap { v =>\n791\t            control.jitFor(v.method) match\n792\t                case Maybe.Present(c) if c.alwaysInlined && v.alwaysRefused =>\n793\t                    Chunk(s\"${v.method}: ${c.bytes}B inlined at all ${c.sites} sites -> ${v.bytes}B refused at all ${v.sites} (${v.reasons.headMaybe.getOrElse(\"no reason\")})\")\n794\t                case Maybe.Present(c) if c.alwaysRefused && v.alwaysInlined =>\n795\t                    Chunk(s\"${v.method}: ${c.bytes}B refused at all ${c.sites} sites -> ${v.bytes}B inlined at all ${v.sites}\")\n796\t                case _ => Chunk.empty\n797\t        }\n798\t\n799\t    /** Methods whose site fractions moved without flipping decisively.\n800\t      *\n801\t      * Reported separately and never as a mechanism: this is the population that produced the irreproducible diffs, so naming it keeps it\n802\t      * visible without letting it explain a delta.\n803\t      */\n804\t    def jitUnstable(control: Run, variant: Run): Chunk[String] =\n805\t        Chunk.from(variant.jit.filter(_.method.startsWith(\"kyo.\"))).flatMap { v =>\n806\t            control.jitFor(v.method) match\n807\t                case Maybe.Present(c) if (c.refused != v.refused || c.inlined != v.inlined) && !(c.alwaysInlined && v.alwaysRefused) && !(c.alwaysRefused && v.alwaysInlined) =>\n808\t                    Chunk(s\"${v.method}: refused ${c.refused}/${c.sites} -> ${v.refused}/${v.sites}\")\n809\t                case _ => Chunk.empty\n810\t        }\n811\t\n812\tend Bench\n813\t"}]},"uuid":"edd2357b-c719-48dc-be16-96df119e8bfb","timestamp":"2026-08-17T15:18:39.278Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/effervescent-painting-backus/kyo-kernel2/.claude/skills/kernel/bench-harness/Bench.scala","content":"import Model.*\nimport kyo.*\nimport scala.util.control.NoStackTrace\n\n/** Runs one leg of a bracket, collecting the whole evidence ladder, and compares stored runs.\n  *\n  * The guards exist because their absence corrupted or wasted a real measurement:\n  *\n  *   - the bracket refuses to run in the tree you commit from\n  *   - designs flip with `git restore --worktree`, which never writes the index (`git checkout <sha> -- <paths>` stages what it restores, so\n  *     an interrupted bracket leaks the comparison design into the next commit)\n  *   - markers are read before and after each leg, so a number carries proof of which design produced it\n  *   - the suite must be green before a leg is measured at all\n  *   - a leg's row count is checked against the benchmark class, retried, then failed; never reported as clean\n  *   - a verdict about the whole class is unreachable from a subset run\n  */\nobject Bench:\n\n    /** Fallback when a session did not measure its own spread. Sessions should always measure it. */\n    val DriftBand = 4.0\n\n    /** Classes the benchmark spends time in that no kernel change can move. */\n    val KnownNoise = Seq(\"BoxesRunTime\", \"java.lang.Integer\", \"jmh_generated\")\n\n    /** JIT refusals that are inherent rather than actionable.\n      *\n      * The reason vocabulary is the compilation log's, verified against a capture: `callee is too large` 1166, `no static binding` 205,\n      * `callee uses too much stack` 173, `not inlineable` 121, `callee's klass not linked yet` 60, `low call site frequency` 19,\n      * `already compiled into a big method` 6, `hot method too big` 5. The strings this filtered on before came from `PrintInlining`'s vocabulary:\n      * \"never executed\" matches nothing the log emits, and \"virtual call\" appears twice in C2, so neither was doing useful work.\n      */\n    def actionableJit(v: InlineSites): Boolean =\n        v.refused > 0 &&\n            // megamorphic by construction: the site sees every arrow kind, and chasing it wastes a session\n            !v.reasons.exists(_.contains(\"no static binding\")) &&\n            // a warmup artifact rather than a decision: the class simply was not linked yet when the\n            // compiler first looked, and the same method inlines fine once it is\n            !v.reasons.exists(_.contains(\"klass not linked\"))\n\n    /** One warmup configuration for every step of a leg.\n      *\n      * The measurement and the evidence runs must reach the same compilation state, or a timing from a well-warmed JVM gets attributed to\n      * inlining decisions captured from a colder one. Ten warmup iterations rather than five because `-prof comp` showed compilation still\n      * running into the first measured iterations at five.\n      */\n    val WarmupIterations  = 10\n    val MeasureIterations = 5\n    val IterationSeconds  = 1\n\n    /** Above this share of the measured window spent compiling, the run had not settled and its score is not a steady-state figure.\n      *\n      * Bounded by evidence rather than validated by it, and the difference is worth stating. Across\n      * every row this campaign has stored that carries `compiler.time.profiled`, 52 of them, the\n      * compile time inside the measured window is a median of 2 ms and a maximum of 9 ms, which is\n      * 0.18% of a 5,000 ms window. The previous limit of 1.0% is 50 ms, so it has never fired and\n      * could not have fired on anything measured here.\n      *\n      * The plan called for tightening it to around the 4 ms of the run that motivated it. That would\n      * be wrong: 8 of those 52 rows sit at or above 4 ms and every one of them is ordinary, so the\n      * tightened guard would be a false-alarm generator. Nor can the right value be found from the\n      * data, because there is no positive case in it: of the 25 rows carrying both an iteration series\n      * and a compile-time figure, none is unsettled by the series criterion, so the two signals have\n      * never been observed to disagree or agree.\n      *\n      * 0.5% is therefore what it is: a little under three times the worst share ever seen, which\n      * leaves room for a genuinely pathological run to trip it while nothing observed does. The signal\n      * actually catching unsettled legs today is `Row.unsettledStart`, from the iteration series, and\n      * this one should not be read as a second working guard until something trips it.\n      */\n    val CompilingShareLimit = 0.5\n\n    val BenchClass  = \"kyo.kernel.bench.ProtoKernelBench\"\n    val BenchSource = \"kyo-kernel2/jvm/src/jmh/scala/kyo/kernel/bench/ProtoKernelBench.scala\"\n    val AsyncProf   = \"/opt/homebrew/opt/async-profiler/lib/libasyncProfiler.dylib\"\n\n    case class BracketFailed(reason: String) extends Exception(reason) with NoStackTrace\n\n    type Fail = Abort[BracketFailed | CommandException | FileReadException | FileFsException]\n\n    /** Lines a JVM prints when it rejected a compile command and ran anyway.\n      *\n      * Exposed rather than buried in the leg runner so it can be tested against the real output that\n      * cost two runs: the JVM prints one line and proceeds, so the measurement looks entirely normal\n      * and tests nothing.\n      */\n    def rejectedCompileCommand(out: String): Chunk[String] =\n        Chunk.from(out.linesIterator.filter(l => l.contains(\"CompileCommand: An error occurred\") || l.contains(\"Error: Method pattern\")).toSeq)\n\n    /** The part of a failed command's output worth showing.\n      *\n      * The whole thing is not. Exercising the red-tree gate for the first time produced a correct\n      * refusal wrapped in several hundred lines of *passing* test names, with the one line naming the\n      * failing test far below the fold, which is a refusal an operator skims past. sbt marks what went\n      * wrong with `[error]` and with scalatest's `*** FAILED ***`; those lines and the tail are the\n      * diagnosis, and the rest is the log.\n      */\n    def failureExcerpt(out: String, tail: Int = 12): String =\n        val lines  = out.linesIterator.toVector\n        val marked = lines.filter(l => l.contains(\"[error]\") || l.contains(\"*** FAILED ***\") || l.contains(\"TESTS FAILED\"))\n        val shown  = (marked.takeRight(20) ++ lines.takeRight(tail)).distinct\n        if shown.isEmpty then lines.takeRight(tail).mkString(\"\\n\")\n        else shown.mkString(\"\\n\") + (if lines.size > shown.size then s\"\\n  (${lines.size} lines of output, the rest of it green)\" else \"\")\n\n    def exec(worktree: Path, command: String*)(using Frame): String < (Async & Fail) =\n        Command(command*).cwd(worktree).redirectErrorStream(true).textWithExitCode.map { (out, exit) =>\n            if exit == ExitCode.Success then out\n            else\n                Abort.fail(BracketFailed(\n                    s\"`${command.mkString(\" \")}` failed with $exit in $worktree:\\n${failureExcerpt(out)}\"\n                ))\n        }\n\n    /** The suite must be green before a leg is measured at all.\n      *\n      * A faster variant whose suite is red is not a result, and this is the gate that says so. It had\n      * never once refused anything, so it was verified by planting a failing test in the throwaway\n      * worktree: `sbt --client` exits 1 on a test failure, `exec` aborts, and the leg never runs.\n      */\n    def requireGreenSuite(worktree: Path, task: String)(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Fail) =\n        exec(worktree, \"sbt\", \"--client\", task).unit\n            .handle(Abort.recoverError[BracketFailed](e =>\n                Abort.fail(BracketFailed(s\"the suite is red, so nothing measured here would be a result.\\n${e.failureOrPanic}\"))\n            ))\n\n    /** Refuses a worktree that is the repository's primary one. A bracket writes over sources; doing that in the tree commits come from is\n      * how uncommitted work and a whole redesign were destroyed.\n      */\n    def requireThrowaway(worktree: Path)(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Fail) =\n        // comparing git dirs only catches the repository's primary worktree, and the tree that\n        // matters is whichever one work happens in, which is always on a branch. A bracket\n        // worktree is created detached, so that is the property to require.\n        exec(worktree, \"git\", \"rev-parse\", \"--abbrev-ref\", \"HEAD\").map(_.trim).map { head =>\n            Abort.when(head != \"HEAD\")(\n                BracketFailed(\n                    s\"$worktree is on branch '$head'; brackets need a detached throwaway worktree (git worktree add --detach <path> <sha>)\"\n                )\n            )\n        }\n\n    /** Discards whatever a previous bracket left behind, so a session starts from a defined tree.\n      *\n      * A throwaway worktree is expected to be dirty after use, since every leg restores sources over it. Requiring it to be pristine would\n      * refuse the normal case; the tree that must never be scribbled on is the one work happens in, and the detached-HEAD guard already\n      * excludes that one.\n      */\n    def resetWorktree(worktree: Path, paths: Seq[String])(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Fail) =\n        exec(worktree, (Seq(\"git\", \"restore\", \"--worktree\", \"--\") ++ paths)*).unit\n\n    /** Asserts a tree carries no uncommitted changes. Used as the post-condition of a reset rather than as an entry requirement. */\n    def requireClean(worktree: Path)(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Fail) =\n        exec(worktree, \"git\", \"status\", \"--porcelain\").map { out =>\n            val dirty = out.linesIterator.filterNot(_.startsWith(\"??\")).toSeq\n            Abort.when(dirty.nonEmpty)(BracketFailed(s\"$worktree has uncommitted changes; commit before measuring:\\n${dirty.mkString(\"\\n\")}\"))\n        }\n\n    /** Hash of the measured sources, so an edit during a run invalidates the leg instead of silently changing what was measured. */\n    def treeHash(worktree: Path, paths: Seq[String])(using Frame): String < (Async & Fail) =\n        // `ls-files -s` reads the index, so an unstaged edit leaves it unchanged and the guard\n        // goes blind to the case it exists for. Diffing the working tree against HEAD sees\n        // every modification, staged or not.\n        for\n            tracked  <- exec(worktree, (Seq(\"git\", \"ls-files\", \"-s\", \"--\") ++ paths)*)\n            modified <- exec(worktree, (Seq(\"git\", \"diff\", \"HEAD\", \"--\") ++ paths)*)\n        yield (tracked + modified).hashCode.toHexString\n\n    /** Measures this machine's run-to-run spread by repeating one row on an unchanged tree.\n      *\n      * No longer on the session path: a bracket estimates its spread from its own replicate legs, on the same tree it measures. This remains\n      * for a single-pair comparison, which cannot replicate and therefore has nothing better to classify against.\n      */\n    def measureDrift(worktree: Path, row: String, samples: Int = 3)(using Frame): Double < (Async & Fail) =\n        val json = worktree / \"bench-drift.json\"\n        def once =\n            exec(worktree, \"sbt\", \"--client\", s\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f 1 -rf json -rff ${json.toString} $BenchClass.$row\")\n                .andThen(json.read).map(parseJmh).map(_.head)\n        Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(1 to samples))(_ => once).map { rs =>\n            val scores = rs.map(_.score)\n            val spread = (scores.max - scores.min) / scores.min * 100\n            // two lucky-quiet runs can report a spread far below the real noise floor, and a band\n            // tighter than the measurement's own error would classify its own uncertainty as a\n            // result. JMH's scoreError is that uncertainty, so the band never goes under it.\n            val ownError = rs.map(r => r.error / r.score * 100).max\n            Math.max(spread, ownError)\n        }\n    end measureDrift\n\n    /** Working-tree-only restore. Never `checkout`, which would also stage. */\n    def restore(worktree: Path, sha: String, paths: Seq[String])(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Fail) =\n        exec(worktree, (Seq(\"git\", \"restore\", s\"--source=$sha\", \"--worktree\", \"--\") ++ paths)*).unit\n\n    def readMarkers(worktree: Path, markers: Seq[(String, String, String)])(using Frame): Chunk[Marker] < (Sync & Fail) =\n        Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(markers)) { (name, pattern, path) =>\n            val file = worktree / path\n            file.exists.map {\n                case false => Marker(name, 0)\n                case true  => file.readLines.map(ls => Marker(name, ls.count(_.contains(pattern))))\n            }\n        }\n\n    /** Counts benchmarks by bare `@Benchmark` lines. Matching the substring also matches `@BenchmarkMode`, which inflates the expectation\n      * and turns a complete run into a reported failure.\n      */\n    def declaredRows(worktree: Path)(using Frame): Int < (Sync & Fail) =\n        (worktree / BenchSource).readLines.map(_.count(_.trim == \"@Benchmark\"))\n\n    // --- JMH json ---------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    case class JmhScore(score: Double, scoreError: Double, scoreUnit: String, rawData: Chunk[Chunk[Double]]) derives Schema\n    case class JmhSecondary(score: Double) derives Schema\n    case class JmhEntry(\n        benchmark: String,\n        mode: String,\n        primaryMetric: JmhScore,\n        secondaryMetrics: Map[String, JmhSecondary]\n    ) derives Schema\n\n    def parseJmh(raw: String)(using Frame): Chunk[Row] < Fail =\n        Json.decode[Chunk[JmhEntry]](raw) match\n            case Result.Failure(e) => Abort.fail(BracketFailed(s\"could not read JMH json: $e\"))\n            case Result.Panic(e)   => Abort.fail(BracketFailed(s\"could not read JMH json: $e\"))\n            case Result.Success(entries) =>\n                entries.map { e =>\n                Row(\n                    name = e.benchmark.split('.').last,\n                    mode = e.mode,\n                    count = e.primaryMetric.rawData.map(_.size).sum,\n                    iterations = Chunk.from(e.primaryMetric.rawData.flatten),\n                    score = e.primaryMetric.primaryScore,\n                    error = e.primaryMetric.safeError,\n                    unit = e.primaryMetric.scoreUnit,\n                    allocPerOp = Maybe.fromOption(e.secondaryMetrics.get(\"gc.alloc.rate.norm\").map(_.score)),\n                    compilerMsProfiled = Maybe.fromOption(e.secondaryMetrics.get(\"compiler.time.profiled\").map(_.score)),\n                    compilerMsTotal = Maybe.fromOption(e.secondaryMetrics.get(\"compiler.time.total\").map(_.score))\n                )\n            }\n\n    extension (s: JmhScore)\n        def primaryScore: Double = s.score\n        def safeError: Double    = if s.scoreError.isNaN then 0.0 else s.scoreError\n\n    // --- evidence parsers -------------------------------------------------------\n\n    // the name column runs to end of line. It was previously spelled as a character class, which\n    // silently truncated every array type the profiler prints: `java.lang.Object[]` arrived as\n    // `java.lang.Object`, so an array allocation and an allocation of its element type became the\n    // same row. On the kernel rows the interesting allocation is the stack's Object[].\n    private val ProfLine = \"\"\"(?m)^.*?(\\d+)\\s+[\\d.]+%\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\S.*?)\\s*$\"\"\".r\n\n    def parseAlloc(raw: String): Chunk[AllocSite] =\n        Chunk.from(ProfLine.findAllMatchIn(raw).map(m => AllocSite(m.group(3), m.group(1).toLong, m.group(2).toLong)).toSeq)\n\n    def parseCpu(raw: String): Chunk[CpuSite] =\n        Chunk.from(ProfLine.findAllMatchIn(raw).map(m => CpuSite(m.group(3), m.group(1).toLong)).toSeq)\n\n    /** The collapsed (FlameGraph folded) allocation view: `frame;frame;...;Class_[i] value`.\n      *\n      * Three things about this format decide whether a parse of it means anything, and all three were\n      * got wrong in the first design of this phase:\n      *\n      *   - **It is root-first.** `frames.head` is `java.lang.Thread.run` on every line. The allocated\n      *     class is the *last* frame and the method that allocated it is the one before that, so both\n      *     are indexed from the leaf end.\n      *   - **The value is a sample count**, because the dump JMH issues carries no `total` option.\n      *     Comparing it against the flat table's bytes is comparing two different quantities, and a\n      *     conservation gate written that way can never pass.\n      *   - **The leaf carries a TLAB marker**, `_[i]` inside and `_[k]` outside, which is part of the\n      *     sample and not part of the class name.\n      */\n    def parseCollapsed(raw: String): Chunk[AllocByMethod] =\n        val entries =\n            raw.linesIterator.flatMap { line =>\n                val cut = line.lastIndexOf(' ')\n                if cut <= 0 then None\n                else\n                    val (stack, value) = (line.substring(0, cut), line.substring(cut + 1).trim)\n                    value.toLongOption.flatMap { n =>\n                        val frames = stack.split(';').filter(_.nonEmpty).map(_.replace('/', '.'))\n                        if frames.length < 2 then None\n                        else\n                            val cls    = frames.last.replaceAll(\"_\\\\[[a-z]\\\\]$\", \"\")\n                            val method = frames(frames.length - 2)\n                            // walk out past the type's own frames. Every Nested on the nested-payload\n                            // row is minted at `Nested$.apply`, which decides nothing; one frame\n                            // further out is who asked for it.\n                            val own  = Seq(cls + \".\", cls + \"$.\")\n                            val site = frames.init.reverseIterator.find(f => !own.exists(f.startsWith)).getOrElse(method)\n                            Some(((cls, method, site), n))\n                    }\n            }.toSeq\n        Chunk.from(\n            entries.groupMapReduce(_._1)(_._2)(_ + _).toSeq\n                .map((k, n) => AllocByMethod(k._1, k._2, n, Maybe.empty, k._3))\n                .sortBy(-_.samples)\n        )\n    end parseCollapsed\n\n    /** Turns the collapsed sample counts into byte estimates using the flat table's bytes per class.\n      *\n      * Only ever an apportionment: the profiler weights each sample by the bytes it stands for, and\n      * that weighting is not recoverable per frame from a sample count. Within one class the sizes\n      * are near-constant, which is what makes the split usable, and it is labelled an estimate.\n      */\n    def apportion(flat: Chunk[AllocSite], byMethod: Chunk[AllocByMethod]): Chunk[AllocByMethod] =\n        val perClass = flat.map(a => a.cls -> a).toMap\n        val totals   = byMethod.groupMapReduce(_.cls)(_.samples)(_ + _)\n        byMethod.map { m =>\n            val estimate =\n                for\n                    site  <- Maybe.fromOption(perClass.get(m.cls))\n                    total <- Maybe.fromOption(totals.get(m.cls)).filter(_ > 0)\n                yield site.bytes.toDouble * m.samples / total\n            m.copy(bytes = estimate)\n        }\n    end apportion\n\n    /** Whether the two views describe the same samples, per class.\n      *\n      * A coverage guard and nothing more: it holds equally for a correct attribution and for one that\n      * assigns every sample of a class to a single arbitrary frame. What it does catch is the parse\n      * losing lines, which is the failure this file has had four times. Both views must come from one\n      * recording, or the comparison is bounded by run-to-run variance instead of by parser\n      * correctness: two recordings of the same planted program differed by 0.25% on the same class.\n      */\n    def allocConservation(flat: Chunk[AllocSite], byMethod: Chunk[AllocByMethod]): Chunk[String] =\n        val totals = byMethod.groupMapReduce(_.cls)(_.samples)(_ + _)\n        flat.filter(_.samples > 0).flatMap { site =>\n            val got = totals.getOrElse(site.cls, 0L)\n            if got == site.samples then Chunk.empty\n            else Chunk(s\"${site.cls}: flat table has ${site.samples} samples, the collapsed view accounts for $got\")\n        }\n    end allocConservation\n\n    // --- one leg ----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def openSession(worktree: Path, driftRow: String)(using Frame): Session < (Async & Fail) =\n        for\n            _    <- requireThrowaway(worktree)\n            // start from a defined tree: a previous bracket leaves its last leg's sources in place\n            _    <- resetWorktree(worktree, Cli.protoPaths)\n            _    <- requireClean(worktree)\n            host <- exec(worktree, \"hostname\").map(_.trim)\n            jvm  <- System.property[String](\"java.version\", \"unknown\")\n            now  <- Clock.now\n        // no drift measurement here any more. A bracket estimates its spread from its own replicate\n        // legs, which is both a better estimate and one taken on the same tree as the measurement;\n        // the old session drift was three extra runs on HEAD sources belonging to neither leg, and\n        // keeping both left two competing noise estimates with the report using the worse one.\n        yield Session(s\"s-${now.toDuration.toMillis}\", host, jvm, 0.0)\n\n    def runLeg(\n        session: Session,\n        worktree: Path,\n        label: String,\n        sha: String,\n        paths: Seq[String],\n        markerSpecs: Seq[(String, String, String)],\n        rows: Seq[String],\n        forks: Int,\n        evidence: Evidence,\n        /** Extra JVM arguments for this leg. Without these a configuration probe is inexpressible and\n          * every falsifier that is a JVM flag has to be run by hand, which is how the two experiments\n          * that diagnosed a live regression were actually run: by a shell script the harness knew\n          * nothing about.\n          */\n        jvmArgs: Seq[String] = Nil,\n        attempts: Int = 3\n    )(using Frame): Run < (Async & Fail) =\n        val selector   = if rows.isEmpty then s\"$BenchClass.*\" else rows.map(r => s\"$BenchClass.$r\").mkString(\" \")\n        val wholeClass = rows.isEmpty\n        val json       = worktree / s\"bench-$label.json\"\n\n        def sbt(task: String) = exec(worktree, \"sbt\", \"--client\", task).map { out =>\n            // A JVM that cannot parse a compile command prints one line and runs anyway, producing a\n            // measurement that looks entirely normal and tests nothing. Two runs were spent that way\n            // before a log line revealed `CompileCommand: An error occurred during parsing`, and both\n            // had already been read as results.\n            if rejectedCompileCommand(out).nonEmpty then\n                Abort.fail(BracketFailed(\n                    \"the JVM rejected a compile command and ran anyway; the measurement tests nothing. \" +\n                        \"Use -XX:CompileCommandFile, which does not have to survive shell and sbt quoting:\\n\" +\n                        rejectedCompileCommand(out).take(3).mkString(\"\\n\")\n                ))\n            else out\n        }\n\n        // pinned on every leg: these rows allocate megabytes per operation, so ergonomic\n        // heap sizing is a live variance source that costs one flag to remove\n        val extraVm = (Seq(\"-Xms4g\", \"-Xmx4g\", \"-XX:+UseG1GC\") ++ jvmArgs).mkString(\" \")\n\n        def measureWith(warmup: Int, n: Int, expected: Int): Chunk[Row] < (Async & Fail) =\n            // the results file is deleted first, every attempt. It is a fixed path per label, so a\n            // run that matched no benchmarks (which JMH exits 0 for, and which is the exact failure\n            // the retry below exists for) would otherwise leave the *previous* attempt's json in\n            // place, and this leg would silently adopt the previous leg's numbers with a row count\n            // that passes every check.\n            json.removeExisting\n                .andThen(sbt(\n                    s\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f $forks -wi $warmup -i $MeasureIterations -r ${IterationSeconds}s \" +\n                        s\"-w ${IterationSeconds}s -prof gc -prof comp -rf json -rff ${json.toString} \" +\n                        \"-jvmArgsAppend \\\"\" + extraVm + \"\\\" \" + selector\n                ))\n                .andThen(json.exists)\n                .map { wrote =>\n                    Abort.when(!wrote)(BracketFailed(\n                        s\"leg $label produced no results file at $json. JMH exits 0 when its selector matches \" +\n                            \"nothing, so this is a run that measured no benchmark rather than a run that failed.\"\n                    ))\n                }\n                .andThen(json.read)\n                .map(parseJmh)\n                .map { parsed =>\n                    val want = if wholeClass then expected else rows.size\n                    if parsed.size == want then parsed\n                    // the first invocation after a recompile can match nothing; a short read is a\n                    // failed run, never a clean one\n                    else if n < attempts then measureWith(warmup, n + 1, expected)\n                    else Abort.fail(BracketFailed(s\"leg $label produced ${parsed.size}/$want rows after $attempts attempts\"))\n                }\n\n        // both views of the allocation profile come out of one recording, which is the only way the\n        // conservation check between them measures the parse rather than run-to-run variance: JMH\n        // stops the profiler once and dumps it twice. `text` is printed inline and carries the bytes;\n        // `collapsed` is written to a file and carries the stacks.\n        val allocDir = worktree / s\"alloc-$label\"\n\n        def profile(event: String, extra: String = \"\") =\n            sbt(\n                s\"\"\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f 1 -wi $WarmupIterations -i 1 -r ${IterationSeconds}s -w ${IterationSeconds}s \"\"\" +\n                    s\"\"\"-prof \"async:libPath=$AsyncProf;event=$event$extra\" $selector\"\"\"\n            )\n\n        /** The collapsed dumps JMH leaves on disk, wherever under `dir` it decided to put them. */\n        def collapsedFiles(using Frame): Chunk[Path] < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException]) =\n            allocDir.exists.map {\n                case false => Chunk.empty[Path]: Chunk[Path] < Any\n                case true =>\n                    allocDir.list.map { entries =>\n                        Kyo.foreach(entries) { e =>\n                            e.list.map(_.filter(_.name.exists(n => n.startsWith(\"collapsed\") && n.endsWith(\".csv\"))))\n                                .handle(Abort.recover[FileFsException](_ => Chunk.empty[Path]))\n                        }.map(_.flatten)\n                    }\n            }\n\n        val logcFile = worktree / s\"logc-$label.xml\"\n\n        /** The only source of inlining decisions.\n          *\n          * The `PrintInlining` run this replaces cost a whole JMH invocation to produce strictly less: no denominator per method, no\n          * deoptimizations, no receiver profiles, and output interleaved across compiler threads so its tree could not be trusted. One run\n          * removed from every leg.\n          */\n        def compilationLog =\n            sbt(\n                s\"\"\"kyo-kernel2JVM/Jmh/run -f 1 -wi $WarmupIterations -i 1 -jvmArgsAppend \"-XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions -XX:+LogCompilation -XX:LogFile=${logcFile.toString}\" $selector\"\"\"\n            ).andThen(logcFile.read).map(LogCompilation.parse)\n\n        for\n            _        <- requireThrowaway(worktree)\n            _        <- restore(worktree, sha, paths)\n            declared <- declaredRows(worktree)\n            // a faster variant whose suite is red is not a result; gate before spending the runs.\n            // this also settles the sources: the build formats on compile, so the baseline below\n            // must be taken after it or the leg invalidates itself on its own formatting\n            _          <- requireGreenSuite(worktree, \"kyo-kernel2JVM/testOnly kyo.kernel.proto.*\")\n            before     <- readMarkers(worktree, markerSpecs)\n            hashBefore <- treeHash(worktree, paths)\n            measured   <- measureWith(WarmupIterations, 1, declared)\n            allocOut <- if evidence == Evidence.Full then profile(\"alloc\", s\";output=text,collapsed;dir=${allocDir.toString}\")\n            else \"\": String < Any\n            allocSites = parseAlloc(allocOut)\n            collapsed <- collapsedFiles.map(fs => Kyo.foreach(fs)(_.read)).map(_.mkString(\"\\n\"))\n            byMethod   = apportion(allocSites, parseCollapsed(collapsed))\n            // the collapsed dump is requested by an option string that has to survive shell, sbt and\n            // JMH quoting. When it does not, JMH runs the profiler anyway and prints a normal-looking\n            // table, so the leg would report allocation with no attribution and nothing would say the\n            // instruction had been dropped. A rejected compile command taught this exact lesson twice.\n            _ <- Abort.when(evidence == Evidence.Full && allocSites.nonEmpty && byMethod.isEmpty)(\n                BracketFailed(\n                    s\"leg $label profiled ${allocSites.size} allocated classes but produced no collapsed view, \" +\n                        s\"so nothing can be attributed to a method. Expected a collapsed-*.csv under $allocDir; \" +\n                        \"check that output=text,collapsed reached JMH.\"\n                )\n            )\n            cpuSites  <- if evidence == Evidence.Full then profile(\"itimer\").map(parseCpu) else Chunk.empty[CpuSite]: Chunk[CpuSite] < Any\n            logc       <- if evidence == Evidence.Full then compilationLog else LogCompilation.Parsed(Chunk.empty, Chunk.empty, 0, Chunk.empty): LogCompilation.Parsed < Any\n            after      <- readMarkers(worktree, markerSpecs)\n            _          <- Abort.when(before != after)(BracketFailed(s\"leg $label markers moved mid-run: $before -> $after\"))\n            hashAfter  <- treeHash(worktree, paths)\n            // sources must not be edited while a run is in flight; if they were, the numbers describe no single tree\n            _   <- Abort.when(hashBefore != hashAfter)(BracketFailed(s\"leg $label sources changed mid-run\"))\n            now <- Clock.now\n        yield Run(\n            id = s\"$label-${sha.take(10)}-${now.toDuration.toMillis}\",\n            session = session,\n            treeHash = hashAfter,\n            label = label,\n            sha = sha,\n            forks = forks,\n            evidence = evidence,\n            wholeClass = wholeClass,\n            declaredRows = declared,\n            markers = before,\n            warmup = WarmupIterations,\n            rows = measured,\n            jit = LogCompilation.inlining(logc),\n            coverage = logc.coverage,\n            jvmArgs = Chunk.from(jvmArgs),\n            alloc = allocSites,\n            allocByMethod = byMethod,\n            cpu = cpuSites,\n            jit_metrics =\n                if evidence == Evidence.Full then\n                    Maybe(LogCompilation.metrics(\n                        logc,\n                        measured.flatMap(_.compilerMsProfiled).sum,\n                        measured.flatMap(_.compilerMsTotal).sum\n                    ))\n                else Maybe.empty,\n            deopts = LogCompilation.deoptSummary(logc),\n            morphism = LogCompilation.morphism(logc),\n            recordedAt = now.show\n        )\n        end for\n    end runLeg\n\n    // --- comparison (pure, over stored runs) ------------------------------------\n\n    def band(control: Run, variant: Run): Double =\n        val measured = Math.max(control.session.driftPercent, variant.session.driftPercent)\n        if measured > 0.0 then measured else DriftBand\n\n    /** Fraction of a run's sampled time in classes no kernel change can move. */\n    def noiseShare(run: Run): Double =\n        val total = run.cpu.map(_.nanos).sum\n        if total == 0L then 0.0\n        else run.cpu.filter(c => KnownNoise.exists(c.method.contains)).map(_.nanos).sum.toDouble / total * 100\n\n    /** Rows whose measured window still contained meaningful compilation.\n      *\n      * Deliberately not corrected by warming longer. A benchmark that needs unusual warmup is reporting something about the code under it,\n      * bigger methods, recompilation churn, or an unstable profile, and warming past it discards the finding. The flag exists so the cause\n      * gets diagnosed.\n      */\n    def stillCompiling(run: Run): Chunk[(String, Double)] =\n        val measuredMs = run.forks * MeasureIterations * IterationSeconds * 1000.0\n        Chunk.from(run.rows.flatMap { r =>\n            r.compilingShare(measuredMs).filter(_ > CompilingShareLimit).map(share => r.name -> share)\n        })\n\n    def sameSession(control: Run, variant: Run): Boolean =\n        control.session.id == variant.session.id\n\n    def compare(control: Run, variant: Run): Comparison =\n        val deltas = Chunk.from(control.rows).flatMap { c =>\n            Chunk.from(variant.row(c.name)).map { v =>\n                val percent = (v.score - c.score) / c.score * 100\n                // never tighter than either leg's own uncertainty. The drift band alone classified a\n                // -9.8% delta as a win on a row whose control leg reported +-15.2%, which is the same\n                // defect the replicate statistic had and had already been fixed there: a threshold\n                // below the measurement's own error classifies that error as a result.\n                val ownError = Math.max(c.relativeError, v.relativeError) * 100\n                val drift    = Math.max(band(control, variant), ownError)\n                val verdict =\n                    // a score whose error is a large fraction of itself cannot support a percentage\n                    if c.error > c.score * 0.5 || c.score <= 0.0 then Verdict.BelowResolution\n                    else if percent < -drift then Verdict.Faster\n                    else if percent > drift then Verdict.Regressed\n                    else Verdict.Flat\n                val allocDelta =\n                    for\n                        ca <- c.allocPerOp\n                        va <- v.allocPerOp\n                    yield va - ca\n                // a row inside the band has not moved, so nothing explains it. Both stored e2e runs\n                // printed a mechanism beside +0.8% and +0.3% deltas, which invites the reader to\n                // believe a cause was found for a difference that is not there.\n                val mechanism =\n                    if verdict == Verdict.Flat || verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution then Chunk.empty\n                    else\n                        Chunk.from(Seq(\n                            allocDelta.filter(d => Math.abs(d) > 1.0).map(d => f\"allocation ${d}%+.0f B/op\"),\n                            jitShift(control, variant).headMaybe.map(m => s\"inlining changed: $m\")\n                        ).flatMap(_.toOption))\n                // a single pair cannot support a t threshold, but it can state the floor it used,\n                // so a flat row is bounded rather than merely quiet\n                Delta(c.name, c, v, percent, verdict, allocDelta, mechanism, Maybe(Resolution(drift, drift * c.score / 100, 0, 0.0)))\n            }\n        }.sortBy(d => (d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution, d.percent))\n        Comparison(control, variant, deltas, jitShift(control, variant))\n    end compare\n\n    /** Family-wise error rate a session is willing to accept across all its rows. */\n    val FamilyAlpha = 0.05\n\n    /** Which design each leg of a bracket measures, in order.\n      *\n      * Control, variant, control, variant, control. Interleaved because measuring all the controls\n      * first and all the variants second confounds the design with everything that drifts over the\n      * session: the variant would always run on a hotter machine, and that bias points the same way\n      * every time. Replicated because a threshold needs a spread estimated from more than one pair,\n      * and three controls against two variants gives three degrees of freedom.\n      *\n      * Pure and separately testable: the ordering is the part worth checking, and checking it should\n      * not cost a half-hour run.\n      */\n    /** One arm of a bracket: the sources it measures and the JVM configuration it measures them under.\n      *\n      * Both, because a comparison is not always between two designs. The campaign's central question,\n      * whether forcing one method to inline recovers a regression, is one design under two JVM\n      * configurations, and a bracket that could only flip shas could not express it. Every such\n      * comparison was therefore run as a single unreplicated leg, which is why they all report a floor\n      * rather than a threshold.\n      */\n    case class Arm(sha: String, jvmArgs: Seq[String] = Nil)\n\n    /** The C V C V C ordering, alternating so machine drift lands in both arms rather than one.\n      *\n      * Generic in what a leg measures because `bracket` compares two `Arm`s and the test that pins\n      * this ordering compares two shas. It was written twice for that reason, once here and once\n      * inline in `bracket`, so the test covered a function the runner did not call and the ordering\n      * that actually ran was pinned by nothing.\n      */\n    def bracketPlan[A](control: A, variant: A, legs: Int = 5): Chunk[(String, A)] =\n        Chunk.from(\n            (0 until Math.max(2, legs)).map { i =>\n                if i % 2 == 0 then (s\"control-${i / 2 + 1}\", control)\n                else (s\"variant-${i / 2 + 1}\", variant)\n            }\n        )\n\n    /** One bracket: every leg of `bracketPlan`, measured in order, split into controls and variants.\n      *\n      * The legs are run through the same `runLeg` as a single measurement, so every guard applies to\n      * each of them: the suite must be green, markers must not move, sources must not change mid-run.\n      */\n    def bracket(\n        session: Session,\n        worktree: Path,\n        control: Arm,\n        variant: Arm,\n        paths: Seq[String],\n        markerSpecs: Seq[(String, String, String)],\n        rows: Seq[String],\n        forks: Int,\n        evidence: Evidence,\n        legs: Int = 5\n    )(using Frame): (Chunk[Run], Chunk[Run]) < (Async & Fail) =\n        Kyo.foreach(bracketPlan(control, variant, legs)) { (label, arm) =>\n            runLeg(session, worktree, label, arm.sha, paths, markerSpecs, rows, forks, evidence, arm.jvmArgs)\n        }.map { ls =>\n            (Chunk.from(ls.filter(_.label.startsWith(\"control\"))), Chunk.from(ls.filter(_.label.startsWith(\"variant\"))))\n        }\n    end bracket\n\n    /** A chain of shas, each step isolating one change from the step before it.\n      *\n      * The reason this exists rather than a second pair: a two-sha comparison measures the difference\n      * between two trees and cannot attribute it, because the partition between the changes inside\n      * that diff was never declared. The skill's worked example is exactly this. Two changes shipped\n      * together, a node-layout change and a currency hoist; the bundle was faster, the win was\n      * credited first to one and then to the other, and both stories were wrong as told. Running the\n      * pieces separately settled it, and running the pieces separately is a chain.\n      *\n      * Each adjacent pair is measured as its own replicated comparison, so every step carries a\n      * threshold rather than a single difference of two numbers.\n      */\n    /** Why a proposed chain is not one, or empty when it is.\n      *\n      * Pure and separate from the runner so the refusal can be tested without a worktree: the whole\n      * point of the guard is that it fires before a single leg is measured.\n      */\n    def requireChain(shas: Seq[String]): Maybe[String] =\n        if shas.size < 3 then\n            Maybe(\n                s\"a chain needs three or more shas; ${shas.size} is a pair, and a pair cannot isolate anything. \" +\n                    \"Use `bracket` for a pair, which reports that it attributes no source-level mechanism.\"\n            )\n        else if shas.distinct.size != shas.size then\n            Maybe(s\"the chain repeats a sha (${shas.diff(shas.distinct).distinct.mkString(\", \")}); a step to the same tree isolates nothing\")\n        else Maybe.empty\n\n    def chain(\n        session: Session,\n        worktree: Path,\n        shas: Seq[String],\n        paths: Seq[String],\n        markerSpecs: Seq[(String, String, String)],\n        rows: Seq[String],\n        forks: Int,\n        evidence: Evidence,\n        legsPerSha: Int = 2\n    )(using Frame): Chunk[(String, Chunk[Run])] < (Async & Fail) =\n        requireChain(shas) match\n        case Maybe.Present(why) => Abort.fail(BracketFailed(why))\n        case _ =>\n            // interleaved rather than grouped: measuring all of sha A then all of sha B puts any\n            // machine drift entirely into the difference between them, which is the mistake the A/A\n            // null's alternating split already exists to avoid\n            val plan =\n                Chunk.from(\n                    (1 to Math.max(2, legsPerSha)).flatMap(rep => shas.zipWithIndex.map((sha, i) => (s\"s$i-$rep\", sha)))\n                )\n            Kyo.foreach(plan) { (label, sha) =>\n                runLeg(session, worktree, label, sha, paths, markerSpecs, rows, forks, evidence)\n            }.map { ls =>\n                Chunk.from(shas.zipWithIndex.map((sha, i) => sha -> Chunk.from(ls.filter(_.label.startsWith(s\"s$i-\")))))\n            }\n    end chain\n\n    /** Compares replicate legs, which is the only shape that can support a threshold.\n      *\n      * A session measures control, variant, control, variant, control.
