Pooling the spread across those replicates is what makes a verdict\n      * answerable for its own uncertainty; the single-pair `compare` above can classify against a drift band but cannot say how small an\n      * effect it would have caught, so every flat row it produces is unbounded.\n      */\n    def compareReplicated(controls: Chunk[Run], variants: Chunk[Run]): Comparison =\n        val rowNames = Chunk.from(controls.headMaybe.map(_.rows.map(_.name)).getOrElse(Chunk.empty))\n        val reps =\n            rowNames.map { name =>\n                Stats.Replicated(\n                    name,\n                    Chunk.from(controls.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.score)),\n                    Chunk.from(variants.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.score)),\n                    // each leg's own relative error, so the threshold can never sit below it\n                    Chunk.from((controls ++ variants).flatMap(_.row(name)).map(r => if r.score == 0.0 then 0.0 else r.error / r.score))\n                )\n            }\n        val common = Stats.commonMode(reps)\n        val deltas =\n            reps.flatMap { r =>\n                for\n                    c0 <- Chunk.from(controls.headMaybe.flatMap(_.row(r.row)))\n                    v0 <- Chunk.from(variants.headMaybe.flatMap(_.row(r.row)))\n                yield\n                    // the rows carried on the delta are the replicate MEANS, not the first leg's\n                    // scores. Showing leg one beside a mean-based percentage let the table read\n                    // \"6.17 -> 6.39 ... +0.0%\", where a reader computing the displayed numbers gets\n                    // +3.6% and the harness is reporting something else entirely.\n                    val c = c0.copy(score = r.controlMean, error = r.pooledSd.getOrElse(c0.error))\n                    val v = v0.copy(score = r.variantMean, error = r.pooledSd.getOrElse(v0.error))\n                    val (verdict, resolution) = Stats.classify(r, FamilyAlpha, rowNames.size)\n                    val allocDelta =\n                        for\n                            ca <- c.allocPerOp\n                            va <- v.allocPerOp\n                        yield va - ca\n                    val mechanism =\n                        if verdict == Verdict.Flat || verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution then Chunk.empty\n                        else\n                            Chunk.from(Seq(\n                                allocDelta.filter(d => Math.abs(d) > 1.0).map(d => f\"allocation ${d}%+.0f B/op\"),\n                                jitShift(controls.head, variants.head).headMaybe.map(m => s\"inlining changed: $m\")\n                            ).flatMap(_.toOption))\n                    Delta(r.row, c, v, r.deltaPercent, verdict, allocDelta, mechanism, resolution)\n            }.sortBy(d => (d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution, d.percent))\n        Comparison(controls.head, variants.head, deltas, jitShift(controls.head, variants.head))\n    end compareReplicated\n\n    /** The A/A null: control legs against each other, through the identical pipeline.\n      *\n      * Any row this classifies, and any mechanism it names, is false by construction. It is the only check here that can fail in the\n      * direction that matters, since every other one asks the harness to stay silent and is therefore satisfied by silence.\n      */\n    def nullComparison(controls: Chunk[Run]): Maybe[Comparison] =\n        // three control legs is the documented session (C V C V C), so requiring four made this\n        // unreachable in the harness's own workflow: the one check that can fail in the direction\n        // that matters never ran.\n        if controls.size < 3 then Maybe.empty\n        else\n            // split by alternation, not by time. Contiguous halves group adjacent-in-time legs, which\n            // understates leg-to-leg spread and puts any warm-up trend entirely in the numerator: over\n            // six legs carrying a 3% monotone trend, contiguous halves report a regression of +1.79%\n            // where alternating halves correctly report flat. The real comparison interleaves control\n            // and variant legs, so the null has to interleave too or it is not measuring the same thing.\n            val indexed = controls.zipWithIndex\n            val a       = Chunk.from(indexed.filter((_, i) => i % 2 == 0).map((r, _) => r))\n            val b       = Chunk.from(indexed.filter((_, i) => i % 2 == 1).map((r, _) => r))\n            if a.isEmpty || b.isEmpty then Maybe.empty else Maybe(compareReplicated(a, b))\n\n    /** Methods whose inlining verdict moved decisively between the two runs.\n      *\n      * Decisive means unanimous on both sides: every site inlined in one leg and every site refused in the other. Anything less is a\n      * fraction that moved, and those move on their own. In a captured pair, 11 of 85 kyo methods carried both verdicts, and for two of them\n      * a single site out of six decided the method's reported verdict. Two runs of one identical comparison named disjoint \"mechanisms\" that\n      * way, one of them a 2-byte method \"refused\" for size. Only a byte count moving with a unanimous flip can be a mechanism, so only that\n      * is reported as one.\n      */\n    def jitShift(control: Run, variant: Run): Chunk[String] =\n        Chunk.from(variant.jit.filter(_.method.startsWith(\"kyo.\"))).flatMap { v =>\n            control.jitFor(v.method) match\n                case Maybe.Present(c) if c.alwaysInlined && v.alwaysRefused =>\n                    Chunk(s\"${v.method}: ${c.bytes}B inlined at all ${c.sites} sites -> ${v.bytes}B refused at all ${v.sites} (${v.reasons.headMaybe.getOrElse(\"no reason\")})\")\n                case Maybe.Present(c) if c.alwaysRefused && v.alwaysInlined =>\n                    Chunk(s\"${v.method}: ${c.bytes}B refused at all ${c.sites} sites -> ${v.bytes}B inlined at all ${v.sites}\")\n                case _ => Chunk.empty\n        }\n\n    /** Methods whose site fractions moved without flipping decisively.\n      *\n      * Reported separately and never as a mechanism: this is the population that produced the irreproducible diffs, so naming it keeps it\n      * visible without letting it explain a delta.\n      */\n    def jitUnstable(control: Run, variant: Run): Chunk[String] =\n        Chunk.from(variant.jit.filter(_.method.startsWith(\"kyo.\"))).flatMap { v =>\n            control.jitFor(v.method) match\n                case Maybe.Present(c) if (c.refused != v.refused || c.inlined != v.inlined) && !(c.alwaysInlined && v.alwaysRefused) && !(c.alwaysRefused && v.alwaysInlined) =>\n                    Chunk(s\"${v.method}: refused ${c.refused}/${c.sites} -> ${v.refused}/${v.sites}\")\n                case _ => Chunk.empty\n        }\n\nend That is what\n211\t      * this did on its first outing against real data, where the row it fires on is one whose timing\n212\t      * does not resolve at all and whose allocation is exact.\n213\t      */\n214\t    enum Quantity derives CanEqual:\n215\t        case Time, Allocation\n216\t\n217\t        def of(r: Row): Maybe[Double] =\n218\t            this match\n219\t                case Time       => Maybe(r.score)\n220\t                case Allocation => r.allocPerOp\n221\t\n222\t        /** Allocation is nearly exact, and \"nearly\" is measured rather than assumed.\n223\t          *\n224\t          * Across four A/A sets of three legs each on identical sources, every row that allocates\n225\t          * kilobytes reproduced its `gc.alloc.rate.norm` to the byte. On the 240,000 B/op effect this has to resolve,\n234\t          * that band is 128 bytes, so it costs nothing that matters.\n235\t          */\n236\t        def resolution(b: Row, i: Row): Double =\n237\t            this match\n238\t                case Time => Math.max(b.relativeError, i.relativeError) * Math.max(b.score, i.score)\n239\t                case Allocation =>\n240\t                    val scale = Math.max(b.allocPerOp.getOrElse(0.0), i.allocPerOp.getOrElse(0.0))\n241\t                    Math.max(1.0, 5e-5 * scale)\n242\t\n243\t        def unit: String = if this == Time then \"\" else \" B/op\"\n244\t    end Quantity\n245\t\n246\t    def quantity(h: Hypothesis): Quantity =\n247\t        h match\n248\t            case Hypothesis.RidesScalarReplacement(_) => Quantity.Allocation\n249\t            case _                                    => Quantity.Time\n250\t\n251\t    /** Adjudicates one falsifier from the run it produced.\n252\t      *\n253\t      * `baseline` is the leg the hypothesis is about, `isolation` the same leg re-run under the flag,\n254\t      * and `target` the number the hypothesis predicts the isolation will reach, in whichever quantity\n255\t      * the hypothesis is about. Model.*\nimport kyo.*\n\n/** Turns a delta into the next experiment, and adjudicates what that experiment returned.\n  *\n  * A comparison says a row moved. What to do about it has been, until now, whatever occurred to the\n  * operator, which is how a redesign came to be credited to the wrong one of its two changes: the\n  * hypothesis was formed from reading the code and never had a falsifier attached. Every entry here\n  * is a hypothesis whose falsifier is a JVM flag, so testing it costs one more run of a configuration\n  * the harness already knows how to issue, and the answer does not depend on anyone's reading.\n  *\n  * Two rules make the answers worth having, and both come from the ways this went wrong before:\n  *\n  *   - **A falsifier that did not take refutes nothing.** `CompileCommand=inline` is a hint; HotSpot\n  *     still refuses on `MaxInlineLevel`, on node budget, or because the method is not compilable.\n  *     A pipeline with no efficacy gate refutes every hypothesis and passes its own acceptance test,\n  *     which is the failure mode this design was reviewed into fixing. So a falsifier whose flag did\n  *     not take is `Inconclusive`, never `Refuted`.\n  *   - **Forcing a callee changes the caller's remaining budget.** A confirm therefore requires that\n  *     the instructed method's verdict moved *and* that nothing else's did. Otherwise the isolation\n  *     changed more than one thing and attributes nothing, which is the same error one level down.\n  */\nobject Investigate:\n\n    /** Which leg the falsifier re-runs. The distinction matters: forcing the variant's refused method\n      * asks whether the refusal caused the loss, forcing the control's asks whether inlining caused\n      * the win, and they are different questions with different answers.\n      */\n    enum Arm derives CanEqual:\n        case Control, Variant\n\n    /** A claim about why a row moved, stated so a JVM flag can contradict it. */\n    enum Hypothesis derives CanEqual:\n        /** The variant stopped inlining this method, and that is the delta. */\n        case StoppedInlining(method: String)\n\n        /** This method is refused for size against a named budget; raising the budget should recover it. */\n        case ExceededBudget(method: String, budget: String, limit: Int)\n\n        /** The win came from inlining rather than from the layout change beside it. */\n        case WinFromInlining(method: String)\n\n        /** The row's allocation depends on scalar replacement, so an enlarged compilation unit that\n          * defeats escape analysis would show up as an allocation cliff.\n          */\n        case RidesScalarReplacement(row: String)\n\n        def target: Maybe[String] =\n            this match\n                case StoppedInlining(m)       => Maybe(m)\n                case ExceededBudget(m, _, _)  => Maybe(m)\n                case WinFromInlining(m)       => Maybe(m)\n                case RidesScalarReplacement(_) => Maybe.empty\n\n        def show: String =\n            this match\n                case StoppedInlining(m)          => s\"$m stopped inlining, and that is the delta\"\n                case ExceededBudget(m, b, l)     => s\"$m exceeded $b ($l bytes)\"\n                case WinFromInlining(m)          => s\"the win came from inlining $m, not from the layout beside it\"\n                case RidesScalarReplacement(row) => s\"$row rides scalar replacement\"\n    end Hypothesis\n\n    /** One runnable experiment: a hypothesis, the leg to re-run, and the flags that contradict it. */\n    case class Falsifier(hypothesis: Hypothesis, arm: Arm, jvmArgs: Seq[String], expectation: String):\n        def show: String = s\"${hypothesis.show}\\n      re-run ${arm.toString.toLowerCase} with ${jvmArgs.mkString(\" \")}\\n      $expectation\"\n\n    /** What a falsifier's run established. */\n    enum Outcome derives CanEqual:\n        /** The flag took and the delta went away: the hypothesis survives its own falsifier. */\n        case Confirmed(detail: String)\n\n        /** The flag took and the delta stayed: the hypothesis is wrong. */\n        case Refuted(detail: String)\n\n        /** Nothing was established, and this is a real result rather than a soft refutation. */\n        case Inconclusive(why: String)\n\n        def show: String =\n            this match\n                case Confirmed(d)    => s\"CONFIRMED: $d\"\n                case Refuted(d)      => s\"REFUTED: $d\"\n                case Inconclusive(w) => s\"INCONCLUSIVE: $w\"\n    end Outcome\n\n    /** The rule table: which experiments a comparison earns.\n      *\n      * Only rows that actually moved generate work, and only methods the compilation log has a\n      * verdict for generate a method-level hypothesis. Two candidate falsifiers from earlier drafts\n      * are deliberately absent: megamorphism, because the log profiles a receiver at 12 sites out of\n      * 5,093 and the hypothesis is not statable from that; and GC ergonomics, because every leg pins\n      * the heap and the collector, so the condition cannot arise without unpinning them.\n      */\n    def falsifiers(c: Comparison): Chunk[Falsifier] =\n        val regressed = c.deltas.filter(_.verdict == Verdict.Regressed)\n        val wins      = c.deltas.filter(_.verdict == Verdict.Faster)\n\n        // a method the control inlined everywhere and the variant refuses everywhere is the\n        // strongest form of this hypothesis, and the only one a single flag can address\n        val stopped =\n            val before = c.control.jit.map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n            c.variant.jit.filter { v =>\n                v.alwaysRefused && before.get(v.method).exists(_.alwaysInlined)\n            }\n        val stoppedFalsifiers =\n            if regressed.isEmpty then Chunk.empty\n            else\n                stopped.map { v =>\n                    Falsifier(\n                        Hypothesis.StoppedInlining(v.method),\n                        Arm.Variant,\n                        Seq(s\"-XX:CompileCommandFile=<file with: inline ${commandForm(v.method)}>\"),\n                        s\"if the ${regressed.size} regressed row(s) recover, the refusal is the cause; if they do not, it is not\"\n                    )\n                }\n\n        // a method sitting just over a budget is the case where raising the budget is a clean\n        // single-variable experiment. Well over it, the flag would change decisions everywhere\n        val budget =\n            c.variant.jit.flatMap { v =>\n                v.nearBudget match\n                    case Maybe.Present(_) if regressed.nonEmpty =>\n                        val (name, limit) = if v.bytes <= 70 then (\"MaxInlineSize\", 35) else (\"FreqInlineSize\", 325)\n                        Chunk(Falsifier(\n                            Hypothesis.ExceededBudget(v.method, name, limit),\n                            Arm.Variant,\n                            Seq(s\"-XX:$name=${v.bytes + 1}\"),\n                            s\"raising only the budget this method is over separates 'too big for the budget' from 'the wrong shape'\"\n                        ))\n                    case _ => Chunk.empty\n            }\n\n        // the cheap direction first: contradicting the win on the control costs one run and can\n        // dissolve the case for the design change entirely\n        val winFalsifiers =\n            if wins.isEmpty then Chunk.empty\n            else\n                val after = c.variant.jit.map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n                c.control.jit.filter(v => v.alwaysRefused && after.get(v.method).exists(_.alwaysInlined)).map { v =>\n                    Falsifier(\n                        Hypothesis.WinFromInlining(v.method),\n                        Arm.Control,\n                        Seq(s\"-XX:CompileCommandFile=<file with: inline ${commandForm(v.method)}>\"),\n                        \"if the control reaches the variant's number, the win is the inlining and not the design\"\n                    )\n                }\n\n        // an allocation change with no timing change, or a large one either way, is the signature\n        // this asks about: an enlarged compilation unit defeating escape analysis\n        val scalar =\n            c.deltas.filter(_.allocDelta.exists(a => Math.abs(a) > 1000.0)).map { d =>\n                Falsifier(\n                    Hypothesis.RidesScalarReplacement(d.row),\n                    Arm.Control,\n                    Seq(\"-XX:-EliminateAllocations\"),\n                    f\"if disabling escape analysis on the control reproduces the variant's ${d.allocDelta.getOrElse(0.0)}%+.0f B/op, \" +\n                        \"the variant destroyed a scalar replacement rather than adding an allocation\"\n                )\n            }\n\n        stoppedFalsifiers ++ budget ++ winFalsifiers ++ scalar\n    end falsifiers\n\n    /** `pkg.Class::method` is how the log names a site; `pkg.Class::method` is also what\n      * CompileCommand wants, but with the class in its own field. Kept as one function so the two\n      * spellings cannot drift apart silently.\n      */\n    def commandForm(logMethod: String): String =\n        logMethod.split(\"::\") match\n            case Array(cls, m) => s\"$cls::$m\"\n            case _             => logMethod\n\n    /** Whether the instructed flag actually changed what it was supposed to change, and nothing else.\n      *\n      * Returns the reason it did not, or empty when it did. Both halves matter: a flag that took at\n      * no site establishes nothing, and a flag that moved five other methods' verdicts as well has\n      * run a different experiment from the one that was asked for.\n      */\n    def efficacy(h: Hypothesis, before: Run, after: Run): Maybe[String] =\n        h.target match\n            case Maybe.Absent => Maybe.empty\n            case Maybe.Present(m) =>\n                val was = before.jit.find(_.method == m)\n                val now = after.jit.find(_.method == m)\n                (was, now) match\n                    case (None, _) => Maybe(s\"$m has no verdict in the baseline leg, so nothing can be said to have moved\")\n                    case (_, None) => Maybe(s\"$m has no verdict in the isolation leg; the method was not compiled there at all\")\n                    case (Some(b), Some(a)) =>\n                        if b.inlined == a.inlined && b.refused == a.refused then\n                            Maybe(\n                                s\"the flag did not take: $m is still ${b.inlined} inlined / ${b.refused} refused. \" +\n                                    \"HotSpot treats an inline command as a hint and still refuses on MaxInlineLevel, node budget, \" +\n                                    \"or a method it cannot compile.\"\n                            )\n                        else\n                            val others =\n                                val map = before.jit.map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n                                after.jit.filter(v => v.method != m && map.get(v.method).exists(b2 => b2.inlined != v.inlined || b2.refused != v.refused))\n                            if others.isEmpty then Maybe.empty\n                            else\n                                Maybe(\n                                    s\"${others.size} other method(s) changed verdict too (${others.take(3).map(_.method).mkString(\", \")}), \" +\n                                        \"so this run changed more than one thing and attributes nothing. Forcing a callee spends the \" +\n                                        \"caller's remaining budget, which is how that happens.\"\n                                )\n    end efficacy\n\n    /** Which measured quantity answers a hypothesis.\n      *\n      * Not a detail: `RidesScalarReplacement` is a claim about bytes per operation, and adjudicating\n      * it against wall clock reads the wrong column and answers a question nobody asked. That is what\n      * this did on its first outing against real data, where the row it fires on is one whose timing\n      * does not resolve at all and whose allocation is exact.\n      */\n    enum Quantity derives CanEqual:\n        case Time, Allocation\n\n        def of(r: Row): Maybe[Double] =\n            this match\n                case Time       => Maybe(r.score)\n                case Allocation => r.allocPerOp\n\n        /** Allocation is nearly exact, and \"nearly\" is measured rather than assumed.\n          *\n          * Across four A/A sets of three legs each on identical sources, every row that allocates\n          * kilobytes reproduced its `gc.alloc.rate.norm` to the byte. The one row that allocates\n          * megabytes did not: `trailingMapsStayLinear` spread 47.8 B on 2.32 MB in one set and 24.2 B\n          * in another, so 2.1e-5 relative at worst.\n          *\n          * A flat one-byte threshold was tried first and it refused the campaign's own escape-analysis\n          * result: the isolation landed 23.8 B from its target on 2.56 MB, which is a reproduction to\n          * six significant figures, and was reported inconclusive. The band is therefore relative,\n          * at 5e-5, a little over twice the worst spread ever observed here, with a one-byte floor so\n          * the rows that really are exact stay exact. On the 240,000 B/op effect this has to resolve,\n          * that band is 128 bytes, so it costs nothing that matters.\n          */\n        def resolution(b: Row, i: Row): Double =\n            this match\n                case Time => Math.max(b.relativeError, i.relativeError) * Math.max(b.score, i.score)\n                case Allocation =>\n                    val scale = Math.max(b.allocPerOp.getOrElse(0.0), i.allocPerOp.getOrElse(0.0))\n                    Math.max(1.0, 5e-5 * scale)\n\n        def unit: String = if this == Time then \"\" else \" B/op\"\n    end Quantity\n\n    def quantity(h: Hypothesis): Quantity =\n        h match\n            case Hypothesis.RidesScalarReplacement(_) => Quantity.Allocation\n            case _                                    => Quantity.Time\n\n    /** Adjudicates one falsifier from the run it produced.\n      *\n      * `baseline` is the leg the hypothesis is about, `isolation` the same leg re-run under the flag,\n      * and `target` the number the hypothesis predicts the isolation will reach, in whichever quantity\n      * the hypothesis is about. The recovery threshold is the legs' own resolution rather than a fixed\n      * percentage, because a leg that cannot resolve the effect cannot answer the question either way,\n      * and saying so is a result.\n      */\n    def adjudicate(\n        f: Falsifier,\n        row: String,\n        baseline: Run,\n        isolation: Run,\n        target: Double\n    ): Outcome =\n        val q = quantity(f.hypothesis)\n        efficacy(f.hypothesis, baseline, isolation) match\n            case Maybe.Present(why) => Outcome.Inconclusive(why)\n            case Maybe.Absent =>\n                (baseline.rows.find(_.name == row), isolation.rows.find(_.name == row)) match\n                    case (Some(bb), Some(ii)) =>\n                        (q.of(bb), q.of(ii)) match\n                            case (Maybe.Present(b), Maybe.Present(i)) =>\n                                val resolution = q.resolution(bb, ii)\n                                val gap        = Math.abs(b - target)\n                                if gap <= resolution then\n                                    Outcome.Inconclusive(\n                                        f\"the baseline is already within its own resolution of the target (${gap}%.2f against +-${resolution}%.2f${q.unit}), \" +\n                                            \"so this experiment could not have separated them whatever it returned\"\n                                    )\n                                else if Math.abs(i - target) <= resolution then\n                                    Outcome.Confirmed(f\"$row moved from ${b}%.2f to ${i}%.2f${q.unit}, reaching ${target}%.2f within +-${resolution}%.2f\")\n                                else if Math.abs(i - b) <= resolution then\n                                    Outcome.Refuted(f\"$row stayed at ${i}%.2f${q.unit} against ${b}%.2f while the flag demonstrably took; the delta is not this\")\n                                else\n                                    Outcome.Inconclusive(\n                                        f\"$row moved from ${b}%.2f to ${i}%.2f${q.unit}, which is neither the target ${target}%.2f nor no move at all\"\n                                    )\n                            case _ =>\n                                Outcome.Inconclusive(\n                                    s\"$row carries no ${if q == Quantity.Allocation then \"allocation figure\" else \"score\"} on one of the legs, \" +\n                                        \"so the quantity this hypothesis is about was never measured\"\n                                )\n                    case _ => Outcome.Inconclusive(s\"$row is missing from one of the two legs\")\n        end match\n    end adjudicate\n\n    /** The report the investigator adds to a comparison. */\n    def render(c: Comparison): String =\n        val fs = falsifiers(c)\n        if fs.isEmpty then \"\"\n        else\n            \"\\n\\nNext experiments, each one run of a configuration this harness already issues:\\n\" +\n                fs.zipWithIndex.map((f, i) => s\"  ${i + 1}. ${f.show}\").mkString(\"\\n\") +\n                \"\\n  A falsifier whose flag did not take refutes nothing; Model.*\nimport caseapp.*\nimport kyo.*\n\n/** Subcommands.\n  *\n  * `run` measures one leg and stores it. `compare` and `show` read stored runs and never measure, which is what makes a reading\n  * reproducible: the same two run ids always produce the same verdict.\n  */\n@AppName(\"bench\")\ncase class RunOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"throwaway worktree to measure in; must not be the primary one\")\n    worktree: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"session id from a previous leg; omit to open a new session, which measures this machine's drift first\")\n    session: Option[String] = None,\n    @HelpMessage(\"row used to measure session drift when opening one\")\n    driftRow: String = \"suspensionBaseline\",\n    @HelpMessage(\"label for this leg, e.g. control or variant\")\n    label: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit whose sources the leg measures\")\n    sha: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"benchmark rows; omit to measure the whole class, which is what a suite-wide claim requires\")\n    row: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"JMH forks; 3 for a claim, 1 for diagnosis\")\n    forks: Int = 3,\n    @HelpMessage(\"evidence to collect: full (default) walks the whole ladder, timing measures only wall clock\")\n    evidence: String = \"full\",\n    @HelpMessage(\"where runs are stored\")\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class CompareOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"run id of a control leg, repeatable; give every control leg of a bracket to get its replicated verdict back\")\n    control: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"run id of a variant leg, repeatable\")\n    variant: List[String],\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class BracketOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"throwaway worktree to measure in; must not be the primary one\")\n    worktree: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit whose sources the control legs measure\")\n    control: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit whose sources the variant legs measure; equal to --control for a configuration comparison\")\n    variant: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"extra JVM args for the control legs, repeatable\")\n    controlJvm: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"extra JVM args for the variant legs, repeatable; this is how a configuration is compared rather than a design\")\n    variantJvm: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"benchmark rows; omit to measure the whole class, which is what a suite-wide claim requires\")\n    row: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"JMH forks per leg; 1 is usually right here since the bracket replicates legs instead\")\n    forks: Int = 1,\n    @HelpMessage(\"legs to run; five gives three controls against two variants, and three degrees of freedom\")\n    legs: Int = 5,\n    evidence: String = \"full\",\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class IngestOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"JMH json files to ingest, in order; label and sha are taken from --label/--sha positionally\")\n    json: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"labels, one per json\")\n    label: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit each json was measured at, one per json (or one for all)\")\n    sha: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"session id to file them under; they must share one to be comparable\")\n    session: String = \"ingested\",\n    @HelpMessage(\"rows the benchmark class declares; a json with fewer is a subset run\")\n    declaredRows: Int = 15,\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class PlanOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"stored runs on the rows you intend to measure; give several legs of the same configuration for a between-leg estimate, which is the quantity a bracket's threshold actually rests on\")\n    from: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"legs the planned bracket would run\")\n    legs: Int = 5,\n    @HelpMessage(\"effect size you need to detect, as a percentage\")\n    target: Double = 5.0,\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class ChainOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"throwaway worktree to measure in; must not be the primary one\")\n    worktree: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commits in order, oldest first, each isolating one change from the one before it; three or more, since two is a pair and isolates nothing\")\n    sha: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"benchmark rows; omit to measure the whole class\")\n    row: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"legs per sha; two gives the chain a spread to threshold against\")\n    legs: Int = 2,\n    forks: Int = 1,\n    evidence: String = \"timing\",\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class ShowOpts(id: String, store: String = \"bench-runs\")\ncase class ListOpts(store: String = \"bench-runs\")\n\nobject Cli:\n\n    val markerSpecs = Seq(\n        (\"SuspendWith\", \"SuspendWith\", \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto/Arrow.scala\"),\n        (\"applyFolded\", \"applyFolded\", \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto/Arrow.scala\"),\n        (\"partial\", \"def partial\", \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto/Eval.scala\")\n    )\n\n    val protoPaths = Seq(\n        \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto\",\n        \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/test/scala/kyo/kernel/proto\"\n    )\n\n    def parseEvidence(s: String)(using Frame): Evidence < Abort[Bench.BracketFailed] =\n        s.toLowerCase match\n            case \"full\"   => Evidence.Full\n            case \"timing\" => Evidence.Timing\n            case other    => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"unknown evidence '$other'; use full or timing\"))\n\n    /** How a failure reaches the operator.\n      *\n      * An expected failure is a diagnosis: one block of text saying what was wrong and what to do,\n      * then exit 1. Left to the default path it arrives instead as `Failure(Bench$BracketFailed: ...)`\n      * followed by the same text again under `Exception in thread \"main\"`, because the app runner\n      * prints the result and then rethrows any Throwable error. Two renders of one problem, both\n      * wearing an internal class name, is what a reader learns to skim.\n      *\n      * A panic is the opposite case and keeps its stack, because it is a defect in this harness rather\n      * than a mistake at the command line, and the frames are the only thing that locates it.\n      */\n    def guard[A](v: A < (Async & Scope & Abort[Any]))(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Scope) =\n        Abort.run[Any](v).map {\n            case Result.Success(_) => ()\n            case Result.Failure(e) =>\n                val message =\n                    e match\n                        case Bench.BracketFailed(reason) => reason\n                        case t: Throwable                => Maybe(t.getMessage).getOrElse(t.toString)\n                        case other                       => other.toString\n                Console.printLine(s\"⛔ $message\").andThen(exit(1))\n            case Result.Panic(t) =>\n                Console.printLine(\"⛔ the harness itself failed, which is a bug in it and not in the command:\")\n                    .andThen(Sync.defer(t.printStackTrace()))\n                    .andThen(exit(2))\n        }\n\n    private def exit(code: Int)(using Frame): Nothing < Sync =\n        // Unsafe: an application entrypoint is the one place a process exit is the correct\n        // expression of a failure, and it is what keeps the diagnosis above from being followed by\n        // the runner's own second rendering of the same error.\n        Sync.defer(java.lang.System.exit(code)).andThen(Sync.defer(throw new IllegalStateException(\"unreachable\")))\n\nend Cli\n\nobject BenchRun extends KyoCaseApp[RunOpts]:\n    run { (opts: RunOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            evidence <- Cli.parseEvidence(opts.evidence)\n            // a session carries the machine's measured drift; reusing one keeps legs comparable,\n            // opening one costs two extra runs and is what makes the band a measurement\n            session <- opts.session match\n                case Some(id) => Store.session(Path(opts.store), id)\n                case None     => Bench.openSession(Path(opts.worktree), opts.driftRow)\n            leg <- Bench.runLeg(\n                session = session,\n                worktree = Path(opts.worktree),\n                label = opts.label,\n                sha = opts.sha,\n                paths = Cli.protoPaths,\n                markerSpecs = Cli.markerSpecs,\n                rows = opts.row,\n                forks = opts.forks,\n                evidence = evidence\n            )\n            file <- Store.save(Path(opts.store), leg)\n            _    <- Console.printLine(s\"stored ${leg.id} (${leg.rows.size} rows, ${leg.evidence}) at $file\")\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchRun\n\n/** Runs a whole bracket and reports it, which is the only shape that can support a threshold.\n  *\n  * A single pair can be classified against a drift band but cannot say how small an effect it would\n  * have caught, so every flat row it produces is unbounded. This replicates instead, and reports the\n  * A/A null first: if the control legs disagree with each other, nothing below that is readable.\n  */\nobject BenchBracket extends KyoCaseApp[BracketOpts]:\n    run { (opts: BracketOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            evidence <- Cli.parseEvidence(opts.evidence)\n            session  <- Bench.openSession(Path(opts.worktree), opts.row.headOption.getOrElse(\"suspensionBaseline\"))\n            legs <- Bench.bracket(\n                session = session,\n                worktree = Path(opts.worktree),\n                control = Bench.Arm(opts.control, opts.controlJvm),\n                variant = Bench.Arm(opts.variant, opts.variantJvm),\n                paths = Cli.protoPaths,\n                markerSpecs = Cli.markerSpecs,\n                rows = opts.row,\n                forks = opts.forks,\n                evidence = evidence,\n                legs = opts.legs\n            )\n            (controls, variants) = legs\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(controls ++ variants)(r => Store.save(Path(opts.store), r).unit)\n            aa  = Bench.nullComparison(controls)\n            cmp = Bench.compareReplicated(controls, variants)\n            // the null's verdict and the steady-state verdict are the same kind of statement, that\n            // the numbers below cannot be read, so they are one banner and one exit code. Reporting\n            // a dirty null as a line of text and exiting 0 is the failure this tool exists to refuse.\n            blockers = Report.nullBlockers(aa, controls.size) ++ Report.blockers(cmp)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                if blockers.isEmpty then Report.nullNote(aa)\n                else\n                    \"\\n\" + \"=\" * 78 + s\"\\n\\u26d4 NOT A VALID SESSION: ${blockers.size} reason(s).\\n\" +\n                        blockers.map(b => s\"  - $b\").mkString(\"\\n\") + \"\\n\" + \"=\" * 78 + \"\\n\"\n            )\n            _ <- Console.printLine(Report.render(cmp))\n            _ <- Abort.when(blockers.nonEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${blockers.size} reason(s) make this session unreadable; see the banner above\")\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchBracket\n\n/** Brings measurements taken outside the harness under it.\n  *\n  * Without this the tool can only speak about runs it produced itself, which is what drove an entire\n  * campaign's worth of verdicts into hand-written python.\n  */\nobject BenchIngest extends KyoCaseApp[IngestOpts]:\n    run { (opts: IngestOpts) =>\n        val session = Session(opts.session, \"ingested\", \"unknown\", 0.0)\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            _ <- Abort.when(opts.json.size != opts.label.size)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${opts.json.size} json files but ${opts.label.size} labels; they must correspond\")\n            )\n            // a third sha for two files means one of the three is going somewhere the operator did\n            // not intend, and the leftover would otherwise be dropped without a word\n            _ <- Abort.when(opts.sha.size != 1 && opts.sha.size != opts.json.size)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(\n                    s\"${opts.json.size} json files but ${opts.sha.size} shas; give one per file, or one for all of them\"\n                )\n            )\n            runs <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.json.zip(opts.label).zipWithIndex)) { case ((j, l), i) =>\n                Ingest.file(\n                    Path(j), l,\n                    opts.sha.lift(i).orElse(opts.sha.headOption).getOrElse(\"unknown\"),\n                    session, Path(opts.store), opts.declaredRows\n                )\n            }\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(runs) { r =>\n                Console.printLine(f\"ingested ${r.id}%-52s ${r.rows.size}%2d rows  ${if r.wholeClass then \"whole class\" else \"SUBSET\"}\")\n            }\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                \"\\nThese are timing-only runs: no markers, no tree hash, no evidence ladder. The report will \" +\n                    \"refuse to attribute any movement in them to a mechanism, which is correct, because nothing \" +\n                    \"about how they were produced was under the harness's control.\"\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchIngest\n\n/** Says what a planned session could detect, before it is spent.\n  *\n  * Three runs were spent reporting a 25% timing regression on a row that resolves to ±22.6% and\n  * cannot support a verdict of that size. Each was believed at the time. This answers that question\n  * from data already stored.\n  */\nobject BenchPlan extends KyoCaseApp[PlanOpts]:\n    run { (opts: PlanOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            priors <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.from))(id => Store.load(Path(opts.store), id))\n            prior = priors.head\n            fs    = Plan.forecast(priors, opts.legs, Bench.FamilyAlpha)\n            blind = Plan.blind(fs, opts.target / 100.0)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                f\"Planning ${opts.legs} legs against a target of ±${opts.target}%.1f%%, from ${prior.rows.size} rows across ${priors.size} prior leg(s).\\n\" +\n                    (if priors.size < 2 then \"One leg only, so the estimate uses within-leg error, which is a different quantity from the between-leg spread a threshold rests on. Give more legs for a real forecast.\\n\" else \"\")\n            )\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(fs)(f => Console.printLine(\"  \" + f.show))\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                if blind.isEmpty then f\"\\nEvery row can resolve ±${opts.target}%.1f%% at this configuration.\"\n                else\n                    f\"\\n\\u26a0\\ufe0f  ${blind.size} row(s) cannot resolve ±${opts.target}%.1f%% and will report flat whatever happens:\\n\" +\n                        blind.map(f => s\"  - ${f.row}\").mkString(\"\\n\") +\n                        \"\\n\\nMore forks will not help: calibration showed tripling them moved the resolution by 0.05 points, \" +\n                        \"because the variance is between legs rather than within them. More legs, or a quieter machine.\"\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchPlan\n\n/** Isolates a source-level mechanism, which a pair of shas structurally cannot.\n  *\n  * A bracket measures the difference between two trees. Attributing that difference to one change\n  * inside it requires the partition to have been declared, and a pair does not declare one. A chain\n  * does: each step is one change, and each adjacent comparison is that change's isolated contribution.\n  */\nobject BenchChain extends KyoCaseApp[ChainOpts]:\n    run { (opts: ChainOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            // before the worktree is touched at all: a chain that is not one should cost nothing\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(Chunk.from(Bench.requireChain(opts.sha).toList))(w =>\n                Abort.fail[Bench.BracketFailed](Bench.BracketFailed(w))\n            )\n            evidence <- Cli.parseEvidence(opts.evidence)\n            session  <- Bench.openSession(Path(opts.worktree), opts.row.headOption.getOrElse(\"suspensionBaseline\"))\n            steps <- Bench.chain(\n                session = session,\n                worktree = Path(opts.worktree),\n                shas = opts.sha,\n                paths = Cli.protoPaths,\n                markerSpecs = Cli.markerSpecs,\n                rows = opts.row,\n                forks = opts.forks,\n                evidence = evidence,\n                legsPerSha = opts.legs\n            )\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(steps.flatMap(_._2))(r => Store.save(Path(opts.store), r).unit)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                s\"Chain of ${steps.size} shas, ${opts.legs} legs each. Each comparison below is one step's \" +\n                    \"isolated contribution, which is the only shape that can carry a source-level mechanism.\\n\"\n            )\n            blockers <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(steps.sliding(2).toSeq).filter(_.size == 2)) { pair =>\n                val (fromSha, fromLegs) = pair(0)\n                val (toSha, toLegs)     = pair(1)\n                val cmp                 = Bench.compareReplicated(fromLegs, toLegs)\n                Console.printLine(s\"\\n${\"-\" * 78}\\n${fromSha.take(10)} -> ${toSha.take(10)}\\n\")\n                    .andThen(Console.printLine(Report.render(cmp, chainLength = steps.size)))\n                    .andThen(Report.blockers(cmp))\n            }.map(_.flatten)\n            _ <- Abort.when(blockers.nonEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${blockers.size} step(s) of the chain are not readable:\\n${blockers.map(b => s\"  - $b\").mkString(\"\\n\")}\")\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchChain\n\nobject BenchCompare extends KyoCaseApp[CompareOpts]:\n    run { (opts: CompareOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            controls <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.control))(id => Store.load(Path(opts.store), id))\n            variants <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.variant))(id => Store.load(Path(opts.store), id))\n            _ <- Abort.when(controls.isEmpty || variants.isEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(\"give at least one --control and one --variant\")\n            )\n            // A bracket's replicated verdict used to be visible only while the bracket ran. Once its\n            // legs were stored, the only thing recoverable from them was the single-pair statistic,\n            // which is the weaker one: on the replicated sweep the pair says five wins and the\n            // replicate statistic says three. So the harness's own principle, that a comparison is a\n            // pure function over records and two run ids always produce the same verdict, held for\n            // the weaker claim and not for the stronger one.\n            replicated = controls.size > 1 || variants.size > 1\n            cmp        = if replicated then Bench.compareReplicated(controls, variants) else Bench.compare(controls.head, variants.head)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                if replicated then\n                    s\"Replicated over ${controls.size} control and ${variants.size} variant leg(s): the threshold below is \" +\n                        \"estimated from the spread between them.\\n\"\n                else\n                    \"One control leg against one variant, so the bound below is the legs' own error and not a \" +\n                        \"threshold estimated from replicates. Pass every leg of a bracket to get its real verdict.\\n\"\n            )\n            _ <- Console.printLine(Report.render(cmp))\n            // a non-steady-state leg fails the run rather than warning inside it. A warning is\n            // something a reader skips; an exit code is not, and this tool exists for a reader who\n            // demonstrably skips them.\n            _ <- Abort.when(Report.blockers(cmp).nonEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${Report.blockers(cmp).size} leg(s) did not reach steady state; the verdicts above are not readable\")\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchCompare\n\nobject BenchShow extends KyoCaseApp[ShowOpts]:\n    run { (opts: ShowOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        Store.load(Path(opts.store), opts.id).map { r =>\n            Console.printLine(\n                s\"\"\"|${r.id}\n                    |  sha ${r.sha} label ${r.label} forks ${r.forks} evidence ${r.evidence}\n                    |  scope ${if r.wholeClass then s\"whole class (${r.declaredRows} rows)\" else s\"${r.rows.size} selected rows\"}\n                    |  markers ${r.markers.map(m => s\"${m.name}=${m.count}\").mkString(\" \")}\n                    |  rows ${r.rows.size}, jit entries ${r.jit.size}, alloc sites ${r.alloc.size}, cpu sites ${r.cpu.size}\"\"\".stripMargin\n            )\n        }\n        )\n    }\nend BenchShow\n\nobject BenchList extends KyoCaseApp[ListOpts]:\n    run { (opts: ListOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        Store.list(Path(opts.store)).map { runs =>\n            if runs.isEmpty then Console.printLine(\"no runs stored\")\n            else\n                Kyo.foreachDiscard(runs.sortBy(_.recordedAt)) { r =>\n                    Console.printLine(f\"${r.id}%-44s ${r.label}%-10s ${r.evidence}%-7s ${r.rows.size}%3d rows  ${r.recordedAt}\")\n                }\n        }\n        )\n    }\nend BenchList\n","numLines":417,"startLine":1,"totalLines":417}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"56e2fdbb-ca73-4797-b6ab-76d78f8f164d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

open = line.indexOf('(')\n55\t            if open < 0 then Maybe.empty\n56\t            else\n57\t                val close = line.indexOf(')', open)\n58\t                if close < 0 then other source of method names, which all use <init>\n65\t                    else Maybe((if before.contains(\".\") && !line.contains(\" \" + name + \"(\") then \"<init>\" else name, line.slice(open, def of(classpath: Path, className: String)(using Frame): Chunk[Method] < (Async & Fail) =\n        Command(\"javap\", \"-c\", \"-p\", \"-cp\", classpath.toString, parse(out)\n        }\n\n    def parse(raw: String): Chunk[Method] =\n        var out     = Chunk.empty[Method]\n        var name    = Maybe.empty[(String, String)]\n        var insns   = Chunk.empty[(Int, String)]\n\n        def flush(): Unit =\n            name.foreach((n, sig) => out = out.append(Method(n, sig, insns)))\n            insns = Chunk.empty\n\n        raw.linesIterator.foreach { line =>\n            declaration(line) match\n                case Maybe.Present(decl) =>\n                    flush()\n                    name = Maybe(decl)\n What changed between two compilations of one method.\n      *\n      * Reports the instructions that arrived and left, not two listings side by side: a reader given both listings does the diff by eye and\n      * gets it wrong, which is the failure mode this whole harness exists to remove.\n      */\n    case class Change(method: String, controlSize: Int, variantSize: Int, added: Chunk[String], removed: Chunk[String]) derives Schema:\n        def sizeDelta: Int = variantSize - controlSize\n\n        /** Whether the change crossed a HotSpot inlining budget, which is the only reason a size change matters on its own. */\n        def crossedBudget: Maybe[String] =\n            val budgets = Seq(35 -> \"MaxInlineSize\", 325 -> \"FreqInlineSize\")\n            Maybe.fromOption(\n                budgets.collectFirst {\n                    case (limit, nm) if controlSize <= limit && variantSize > limit  => s\"grew past $nm ($limit)\"\n                    case (limit, nm) if controlSize > limit && variantSize <= limit  => s\"dropped below $nm ($limit)\"\n                }\n            )\n\n        def show: String =\n            val budget = crossedBudget.map(b => s\", $b\").getOrElse(\"\")\n            val plus   = if added.isEmpty then \"\" else s\" +${added.mkString(\",\")}\"\n            val minus  = if removed.isEmpty then \"\" else s\" -${removed.mkString(\",\")}\"\n            f\"$method%s ${controlSize}B -> ${variantSize}B ($sizeDelta%+d)$budget$plus$minus\"\n    end Change\n\n    /** Methods whose compiled form differs, by name. Methods identical in both are omitted rather than listed as unchanged. */\n    def diff(control: Chunk[Method], variant: Chunk[Method]): Chunk[Change] =\n        val byName = control.map(m => (m.name + m.signature) -> m).toMap\n        Chunk.from(\n            variant.flatMap { v =>\n                byName.get(v.name + v.signature).flatMap { c =>\n                    val cm = c.mnemonics\n                    val vm = v.mnemonics\n                    if cm == vm && c.size == v.size then None\n                    else\n                        // multiset difference: an instruction appearing three times in one and twice\n                        // in the other is one removal, not zero\n                        Some(Change(\n                            method = v.name + v.signature,\n                            controlSize = c.size,\n                            variantSize = v.size,\n                            added = Chunk.from(vm.diff(cm).distinct),\n                            removed = Chunk.from(cm.diff(vm).distinct)\n                        ))\n                }\n            }\n        )\n    end diff\n\n    /** Cross-checks computed sizes against HotSpot's own `bytes` attribute from the compilation log.\n      *\n      * Two independent derivations of the same number. Load before changing kernel sources, reviewing kernel code, or designing kernel features. Composition first, the evaluator second; casts and other concessions only when measured, justified, and protected.\n---\n\n# Working on the kernel\n\nThis skill captures how kernel work is done, distilled from the sessions that built the Arrow-based kernel. It is\nthe standard the code is held to, not a suggestion. Scope for now: design ethos, type safety, how concessions are\nmade, and how performance claims are established. Other areas (porting, docs) come later.\n\n## Composition first, the evaluator second\n\nA kernel computation is a value built by composition. The evaluator is an accelerator for those values, not the\ndefinition of what they mean. Every piece of evaluator behavior must be the operational reading of an equation you\ncan write in the public combinators; if you cannot write the equation, you do not understand the case yet, and no\namount of machine choreography will substitute.\n\nWorking rules that follow from this:\n\n- **When the evaluator has a gap, write the equation first.** In terms of `map`, `Handle`, the segment values, the\n  existing adapters. Then realize each piece with values the evaluator already has. Model.*\nimport kyo.*\n\n/** Turns a JMH json produced outside the harness into a stored `Run`.\n  *\n  * This exists because its absence caused the worst failure of the campaign. Every comparison the\n  * harness can make requires a `Run`, and a `Run` could only be built by `runLeg`. So a measurement\n  * taken with a raw `sbt Jmh/run`, which is what every isolation experiment needs, had no path into\n  * `Bench.compare` or `Report.render`. Faced with that, the operator computed the verdicts by hand in\n  * python: deltas, thresholds, significance screens, all of it outside the tool built to prevent\n  * exactly that. Four experiments produced conclusions the harness never saw.\n  *\n  * An ingested run is deliberately weaker than a measured leg, and says so:\n  *\n  *   - `evidence = Timing`, so the report states that no movement here is attributed\n  *   - no markers, so it cannot prove which design produced it\n  *   - `treeHash` records the file it came from rather than a tree, so it cannot claim a clean tree\n  *\n  * Those are not omissions to fix later. An ingested run genuinely does not know those things, and\n  * the report must not imply otherwise.\n  */\nobject Ingest:\n\n    case class Failed(what: String) extends Exception(what) with scala.util.control.NoStackTrace\n\n    /** Build a `Run` from a JMH json document.\n      *\n      * `declaredRows` is what the benchmark class declares. A json holding fewer rows than that is a\n      * subset run, and the report already refuses to make a suite-wide claim from one; getting this\n      * wrong in the permissive direction is how a four-row subset once passed as a clean suite.\n      */\n    def run(\n        raw: String,\n        label: String,\n        sha: String,\n        session: Session,\n        source: String,\n        declaredRows: Int\n    )(using Frame): Run < Bench.Fail =\n        Bench.parseJmh(raw).map { rows =>\n            if rows.isEmpty then Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"$source holds no benchmark rows\"))\n            else\n                Run(\n                    id = s\"$label-${sha.take(10)}-${source.hashCode.toHexString}\",\n                    session = session,\n                    label = label,\n                    sha = sha,\n                    // not a tree hash: this run was not produced from a tree this harness controlled,\n                    // and pretending otherwise would let it claim a guard it never passed\n                    treeHash = s\"ingested:$source\",\n                    forks = 1,\n                    evidence = Evidence.Timing,\n                    wholeClass = rows.size >= declaredRows,\n                    declaredRows = declaredRows,\n                    markers = Chunk.empty,\n                    warmup = Bench.WarmupIterations,\n                    jit_metrics = Maybe.empty,\n                    rows = rows,\n                    jit = Chunk.empty,\n                    coverage = Chunk.empty,\n                    alloc = Chunk.empty, allocByMethod = Chunk.empty,\n                    cpu = Chunk.empty,\n                    deopts = Chunk.empty,\n                    morphism = Chunk.empty,\n                    recordedAt = source\n                )\n        }\n\n    /** Reads a json file and stores the resulting run. */\n    def file(\n        path: Path,\n        label: String,\n        sha: String,\n        session: Session,\n        store: Path,\n        declaredRows: Int\n    )(using Frame): Run < (Async & Bench.Fail & Abort[FileWriteException]) =\n        path.read.map { raw =>\n            run(raw, label, sha, session, path.name.getOrElse(path.toString), declaredRows).map { r =>\n                Store.save(store, r).andThen(r)\n            }\n        }\n\nend Ingest\n","numLines":85,"startLine":1,"totalLines":85}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"378f98ea-78d0-4605-a8b8-8d28394f1218","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

{"parentUuid":"cdb537ba-42ad-4fdf-8e82-e73e3464a7b4","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"af5a83bcca1649bc3","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Ce8YznaHh8MQbRTYG27vp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I have what I need. Here is the review.\n\n---\n\n# Held-out review: `IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md`\n\nEverything below is grounded in the sources, the stores under `bench-results/`, and the defect ledger. I re-derived the replicated sweep's thresholds from its five stored legs independently and reproduced the report's numbers exactly (±59.94, ±12.63, ±14.43, ±3.93, ±3.62, ±5.77), so the arithmetic underneath my claims is checked against the tool's own, not taken from its writeups.\n\n## 1. Verdict on the thesis: half right, and the wrong half is load-bearing\n\n**The claim.** \"The harness is good at refusing and weak at volunteering\" (`IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md:5`), and the remaining value is \"converting data already in the store into statements the report makes out loud\" (`:16-18`).\n\n**The ledger does not support it.** Classifying all 29 entries in `tool-defects.md` by failure shape:\n\n- **The tool said something wrong or silently substituted a weaker thing:** 10 (leg one beside a mean-based delta), 12 (no floor, classified noise as a win), 18 (adjudicated bytes-per-op on wall clock), 19 (band refused a six-figure reproduction), 25 (config not recorded), 27 (silently gave the single-pair statistic where the replicate statistic existed), 29 (`BenchPlan` wrong three ways). **Seven.**\n- **A guard that did not guard, or an input it accepted wrongly:** 6, 14, 15, 16, 20, 21, 22, 24. **Eight.**\n- **Capability it simply lacked:** 1, 2, 4, 11, 13, 17. **Six.**\n- **Genuinely \"had the data, did not say it\":** 3 (budget ranking), 8 (resolution after the fact), 28 (only the worst resolution). **Three**, and 26 (precision) is arguably a fourth.\n\nSo the plan's diagnosis covers roughly one item in eight. The dominant historical failure is not silence; it is **a confident statement that was wrong, or was not the statement it claimed to be**. And note where the last three were found: defects 27, 28 and 29 all came from the section `tool-defects.md:213` calls \"validating one part of the tool against another.\" Defects 20-23 came from exercising guards that had never fired. Defects 14-16 came from running the CLI wrong on purpose.\n\n**Why that matters for this plan specifically.** A1, A2, A3 and A5 each add a *new derived claim* to the report. Every one of them lands in the category that has produced seven wrong outputs, and the plan proposes **zero** new cross-validation, no adversarial exercise, no A/A-equivalent for any of them. The section titled \"What this plan deliberately does not propose\" (`:142-149`) says \"No new statistics\" and \"Nothing that makes a verdict easier to obtain\" — but a new derived claim is a new estimator whether or not it has a t-statistic in it, and A5 in particular promotes `BenchPlan` (wrong in three independent ways as of defect 29, validated against exactly **one** bracket) from opt-in to always-on.\n\n**And the \"refuses well\" half is not true either.** Concretely:\n\n`Bench.nullComparison` and `Report.nullBlockers` are called from exactly one place in the whole harness: `Cli.scala:210` and `Cli.scala:215`, inside `BenchBracket`. `BenchCompare` (`Cli.scala:351-386`) does not run the A/A null. `BenchChain` (`Cli.scala:309-349`) does not run it either. Consequences:\n\n- Re-reading a stored bracket through `bench compare --control ×3 --variant ×2` reproduces the replicated verdict — defect 27's fix works — and **silently drops the A/A null**, which `Bench.scala:760-763` calls \"the only check here that can fail in the direction that matters.\" This is defect 27 one level up: the strongest statement still exists only in the scrollback of the run that produced it.\n- `bench chain` never checks itself on any step, at any leg count.\n\nThat is a first-order refusal gap, it is worth more than anything in section A, and the plan's author cannot see it because the thesis told them refusals were the finished part.\n\n**Verdict: the thesis is a third of the story, and it points work at the tool's strongest surface (rendering) while leaving its actual failure mode (wrong derived statements, and one missing refusal) untouched.**\n\n---\n\n## 2. Per-item assessment\n\n### A1 — flag when the largest movements are the unresolvable ones — **KEEP, REWORK; the evidence and the acceptance are both wrong**\n\nThe mechanism is real and I verified it. `Bench.compare`/`compareReplicated` sort by **signed** percent (`Bench.scala:589`, `Bench.scala:756`), so the largest speedup is at the top of the table and the largest regression at the bottom. On the replicated sweep the table opens with `emittingClauses -12.5` and closes fifteen rows later with `trailingMaps +43.2`. A reader scanning by magnitude has to read both ends.\n\nBut the plan's evidence is factually wrong. Recomputed from `bench-results/sweep-replicated/runs/`:\n\n| row | delta | resolution | verdict |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `trailingMapsStayLinear` | **+43.2%** | ±59.94% | Flat |\n| `emittingClausesPayRegionRebuild` | −12.5% | ±12.63% | Flat |\n| `handleLoopAnswersInPlace` | −10.7% | ±14.43% | Flat |\n\nThe largest delta on the board is **+43.2%**, not −12.5%. The plan says \"the two biggest deltas on the board, −12.5% and −10.7%\" (`:28-29`), inherited verbatim from `bench-results/sweep-replicated/RESULT.md:29` and `WORK.md:49`. The top **three** by |delta| are all unresolvable. The acceptance as written — \"Fires on the replicated sweep naming both rows\" (`:35`) — would be implemented as a test asserting two names on a case that has three, i.e. the acceptance test would pin an under-firing implementation on the tool's own canonical fixture.\n\nThere is also a cheaper intervention the plan does not consider: the table ordering itself is the defect. Sorting by |delta| within verdict class, or adding a magnitude rank, is structural and unskippable. The plan's chosen mechanism — a sentence after the table — is the mechanism the campaign has already established does not reach this reader (`Store.scala:96-101`: \"a placement that assumes the reader is disciplined. The operator this tool exists for is demonstrably not\").\n\n**Rework:** fix the acceptance to three rows; make it a table property (ordering or a column), not appended prose.\n\n### A2 — cross-reference a row against its own history — **CUT**\n\nThe plan flags it as speculative (`:51-52`). It is worse than speculative; it is not implementable against the data that exists, and if forced through it would produce alarms nobody can discharge.\n\n1. **The four readings are not in one store.** The −12.5% is in `bench-results/sweep-replicated/runs/`; the −9.78% sweep pair and the −9.5% `-wi 25` reading are in `bench-results/store/runs/`. There are nine separate `runs/` directories under `bench-results/` and no cross-store index. The acceptance \"On the current store it names `emittingClausesPayRegionRebuild`\" (`:48`) is unsatisfiable from any single store as the term is used everywhere else in the harness (`--store <path>`, `Store.requireStore`, `Store.scala:53-59`).\n\n2. **The store cannot express *why* those readings differ, on precisely the runs that matter.** Every one of the twelve runs in `bench-results/store/runs/` has `jvmArgs` absent. That includes `sweep-forced`, `e1-new-f600`, `e2-new-forced`, `e4-default-noEA` and `e4-forced-noEA` — five runs whose entire identity is a JVM configuration the record does not hold. This is defect 25 as recorded: \"the configuration is unrecoverable rather than merely unstated\" (`tool-defects.md:203-204`). A history check over that store compares `sweep-default` against `sweep-forced` and sees two readings of one row under \"identical\" recorded conditions that in fact differ by a forced inline. It will fire, correctly by its own rule, on a difference the store makes impossible to explain away.\n\n3. **The negative acceptance is probably false.** \"does not name `continuationBodiesFuse`, which has been consistent across every measurement\" (`:48-49`). `continuationBodiesFuse` has produced −4.87% (original sweep), −6.8% (bracket1), −7.1% (replication), −0.7% (tier3 variant 3, `WORK.md:107-111`), and −17.4% (DIS-2 under `FreqInlineSize=600`, `WORK.md:234-236`). A naive self-disagreement check names it loudest of all. Making it *not* fire requires conditioning on sha, jvmArgs, row-subset, warmup and session — and the store is missing or wrong on three of those five for the historical runs.\n\n4. **It contradicts a refusal the tool already has.** `Report.render` refuses cross-session comparison outright (`Store.scala:391-396`: \"these runs are from different sessions, so the deltas below are not comparable\"). A2 is a cross-session comparison wearing a different hat.\n\nThe plan says \"Prefer under-firing.\" Under-firing here means never firing, because the only case in the store that would fire is one the store cannot substantiate. **Cut it.** If history is wanted, the prerequisite is a store index plus complete configuration provenance, which is B3's neighbourhood, not A's.\n\n### A3 — per-row noise share — **CUT AS WRITTEN; there is a real and better defect underneath it**\n\nThe plan's premise is that per-row attribution is derivable from stored profiles. It is not, on two independent counts.\n\n**There is no CPU profile in any campaign store.** I enumerated every stored run:\n\n```\nbench-results/{aa-store,aa-store2,aa-f3,bracket-store,tier3-store,\n               sweep-replicated,c4-store2,store}/runs/*.json   -> cpu = 0, evidence = Timing\nqa-artifacts/store/runs/qa-{control,variant}-*.json            -> cpu = 12 and 11, evidence = Full\n```\n\nForty-five of forty-seven stored runs carry no profile at all. The only two that do are the QA fixtures, single-row subset runs on `nestedPayloadsUnwrapInMaps`. The acceptance \"Names `nestedPayloadsUnwrapInMaps` from the stored capture with a share near 70%\" (`:65`) cannot be met: the 70% figure was computed by hand from `qa-artifacts/qa-cpu.txt`, a raw 28-frame async-profiler table that is not in any `Run`.\n\n**The model has no place to put a per-row attribution even if the profile existed.** `Run.cpu` is `Chunk[CpuSite]` and `CpuSite` is `(method, nanos)` (`Model.scala:217`, `Model.scala:327`) — one flat list per *leg*, no row key. `runLeg` collects it with `profile(\"itimer\")` over `$selector` (`Bench.scala:485`, `:426-430`), and `parseCpu` (`Bench.scala:252-253`) flattens whatever tables the invocation printed into one list. On a whole-class Full-evidence leg that would concatenate fifteen profile tables with no way to separate them — a latent defect that has never fired only because every whole-class run in the campaign was `Timing`. A3 is therefore not \"convert data already in the store\"; it is a schema change plus a re-measurement, which is the one thing the plan's thesis claims section A avoids.\n\n**What is actually broken, and is worth fixing.** `Bench.KnownNoise = Seq(\"BoxesRunTime\", \"java.lang.Integer\", \"jmh_generated\")` (`Bench.scala:23`). On the one real profile in the repository, that list matches `boxToInteger` at 29.1% and **nothing else**. The benchmark's own generated code is named `kyo.kernel.bench.ProtoKernelBench.loop$9` (17.14%), `...run$39` (13.23%), `ProtoKernelBench$.ask` (11.06%) and `ProtoKernelBench$$anon$95.<init>` (6.72%) — no `jmh_generated` substring anywhere. So `Bench.noiseShare` reports **29%** where the true non-kernel share is **70%**, and `Store.scala:398-401` prints that 29% under the sentence \"% of sampled time is in classes no kernel change can move.\"\n\nThat is a wrong number the tool volunteers, understated by 41 points, biased in the direction that makes the kernel look more relevant than it is — the exact bias this campaign spent three independent readings correcting (`WORK.md:288-291`, `bench-results/premises/RESULT.md:70-77`, `bench-results/in2/RESULT.md:70-76`).\n\nAnd it is open defect 9 caught in the act. The test that covers this is `BenchTest.scala:120-121`, whose fixture is two frames: one `BoxesRunTime` and one `kyo.kernel.proto.Eval$.loop`. It contains no `ProtoKernelBench` frame, so it cannot fail on the real failure mode. \"Every fixture in this suite was generated by the same understanding that wrote the code under it\" (`tool-defects.md:90-91`) — here is the live instance, still costing 41 points on the only profile that exists.\n\n**Replace A3 with:** extend `KnownNoise` to cover the benchmark's own generated code (`kyo.kernel.bench.`), make the note name its top contributing frames rather than emit a bare percentage, and add a fixture drawn from `qa-artifacts/qa-cpu.txt` rather than authored. That is one constant, one render change, one non-authored fixture, and it converts a wrong volunteered statement into a right one. It is a strictly better item than A3, and it is small.\n\n### A4 — say when a budget candidate is not kernel code — **KEEP, but the premise is wrong and the item is bigger than stated**\n\nI verified the fact: `ProtoKernelBench::run$56`, 379 B, refused 10/10, does top the ranking (`bench-results/premises/RESULT.md:54`, `:70-73`). Worth noting the sort key is `-refused` (`LogCompilation.scala:372`), i.e. refused *site count*, not proximity to budget — so \"the budget-proximity ranking\" is a slight misnomer, and `run$56` tops it because it is refused at ten sites, not because it is 1.17x over.\n\nThe premise that fails is \"**The tool ranks it helpfully** and never mentions that optimizing it would be optimizing the benchmark\" (`:71-72`). It does not rank it anywhere the operator can see. `LogCompilation.budgetCandidates` has exactly two call sites in the repository: itself, and a `println` in a test main at `LogCompilationTest.scala:294`. No CLI subcommand exposes it (`Cli.scala` defines `run`, `bracket`, `ingest`, `plan`, `chain`, `compare`, `show`, `list` — none surfaces inlining state). `Report.render` never calls it. `Investigate.falsifiers` uses `nearBudget` directly, but only when `regressed.nonEmpty` (`Investigate.scala:121`) and only on legs carrying JIT data — neither held on the replicated sweep, which is `Timing` evidence with `jit = 0` on all five legs.\n\nSo `run$56` reached `premises/RESULT.md` by hand, exactly like the 70% figure did. **Keep A4, and widen it:** the ranking needs a CLI surface at all, with the kernel/non-kernel partition built in from the start. Adding a label to a function nobody can call is busywork; adding the command is the item.\n\n### A5 — run `BenchPlan` automatically before a bracket — **KEEP, REWORK; it needs a selection rule the plan does not state**\n\nThe motivation is sound and the sunk cost is real (`Plan.scala:5-12`, defect 8). Point it at a whole store and it pools legs across shas, JVM configurations, sessions and row-subsets into one \"arm\" spread. On `bench-results/store/runs/` that means pooling `sweep-default` with `sweep-forced` (a forced inline, unrecorded), and `e5-tier1` with `e5-tier2` (two different designs), and emitting a confident ±X per row. That is exactly the mechanism the tool needs, and it was built.\n11\t\n12\t| selector | selects on | wired into production? |\n13\t|---|---|---|\n14\t| `LogCompilation.diffVerdicts` | verdict changed between legs | yes, via `Comparison.jitChanges` |\n15\t| `Bench.actionableJit` | refusal worth chasing vs inherent | yes, 1 call |\n16\t| `InlineSites.nearBudget` | method sits close to a budget | yes, 1 call, inside `Investigate` |\n17\t| **`LogCompilation.budgetCandidates`** | refusals ranked by site count | **no** |\n18\t| **`Bytecode.Change.crossedBudget`** | size change flipped an inlining budget | **no** |\n19\t| **`Bytecode.diff` / `Bytecode.of`** | per-method sizes between two trees | **no** |\n20\t| **`LogCompilation.efficacy`** | did the instructed flag actually take | **no** |\n21\t| **`LogCompilation.unprofiledSites`** | sites with no receiver data | **no** |\n22\t\n23\t**Three wired, five not.** Every one of the five has tests. `Bytecode` is an entire tested module with\n24\tzero production call sites. `unprofiledSites` has no caller anywhere but its own definition.\n25\t\n26\tEvery throwaway probe written during this campaign called one of the five. That is the whole\n27\texplanation, and it is not a discipline failure: **the logic was on no code path, so no amount of\n28\tremembering would have surfaced it.** Writing a probe was the only way to reach it.\n29\t\n30\t## The rule this yields\n31\t\n32\t> **A flag must carry its own evidence.** If the report says a row is unexplained, that paragraph\n33\t> contains the evidence it is standing on. If it proposes an experiment, it can score that experiment.\n34\t> If a guard fails a leg, the failure names what did not reconcile. **No output may instruct the\n35\t> operator to go and look something up.**\n36\t\n37\tThe tool violates this in its own text today:\n38\t\n39\t```\n40\t⚠️  Moved with nothing in the evidence behind it, so the cause is not known yet:\n41\t  - continuationBodiesFuse: check allocation sites and the inlining log before proposing a mechanism\n42\t```\n43\t\n44\tIt holds `alloc`, `allocByMethod`, `jit` (944 entries), `cpu` and `deopts` for both legs, and responds\n45\tto \"I cannot explain this\" by assigning homework.\n46\t\n47\t**Acceptance test for the whole plan:** grep the renderers for imperatives — *check, look at, verify,\n48\tsee the, diagnose*. Each surviving one is a place the tool knows something and delegated it back.\n49\t\n50\t## The changes\n51\t\n52\t### 1. Wire `efficacy` into the comparison report\n53\tThe highest-value item. It is the guard that stopped DIS-2 being credited with a −17.4% win the flag\n54\tnever caused, and it fires today only if someone writes a probe. When two legs differ in `jvmArgs`,\n55\tthe report must state whether the instructed method's verdict actually moved, and whether anything\n56\telse moved with it. **Acceptance:** the stored DIS-2 pair reports that `dispatch$1` is refused in both\n57\tlogs, without a probe.\n58\t\n59\t### 2. Give the unexplained-row flag its evidence\n60\tReplace the homework line with what exists: the row's own allocation delta (per-row, real), the leg's\n61\tactionable refusals and near-budget methods, **explicitly labelled leg-wide**, and then the honest\n62\tstatement that a whole-class leg cannot attribute inlining to one row. **This is a hard limit, not an\n63\tomission:** fifteen rows produce one compilation log and the model has no row→method mapping. Saying\n64\tso is the fix; inventing the join would be the tool asserting what it cannot know.\n65\t\n66\t### 3. `Report.renderRun`, used by `run` and `show`\n67\t`run` spends four JMH invocations building a 22-field `Run` and prints one line. `show` renders 944 jit\n68\tentries as the number 944. One renderer, two call sites, gives homes to `budgetCandidates`,\n69\t`unprofiledSites`, the per-leg JIT cost table, allocation attribution, and `coverage`.\n70\t**Open question for the reviewer:** a bracket calls `runLeg` five times, so a full per-leg render would\n71\temit five reports before the comparison. Suppress under `bracket`, or print a digest?\n72\t\n73\t### 4. Fix `KnownNoise`, and name frames instead of one aggregate\n74\t`Seq(\"BoxesRunTime\", \"java.lang.Integer\", \"jmh_generated\")` matches `boxToInteger` and nothing else on\n75\tthe only real profile in the repository. The benchmark's own generated code is `ProtoKernelBench.loop$9`\n76\t(17.1%), `run$39` (13.2%), `ask` (11.1%). So the report prints **29% where the truth is 70%**,\n77\tunderstated in the direction that flatters the kernel. Its fixture is two authored frames with no\n78\t`ProtoKernelBench` in them, so it cannot fail. Annotate `resolves` with which term binds it\n87\t`Stats.threshold` is `max(t·se, ownError·controlMean)` and both terms are already computed. Seven of\n88\tfifteen rows in the replicated sweep are floor-bound, including `handleLoopAnswersInPlace` at −10.7%\n89\twith a ±14.4% threshold set **entirely** by the own-error floor against a ±8.2% spread term — the row\n90\twhose demotion turned five wins into three. `±14.4% (own error)` is fixed by forks; `±12.6% (spread)`\n91\tby more legs. `Plan.scala` currently tells the operator, unconditionally, that forks do not help.\n92\t\n93\t### 7. Capture method sizes in `runLeg`, so `crossedBudget` has two sides\n94\tThe only item needing new capture. `Bytecode.of` reads compiled classes at analysis time and nothing\n95\tcalls it, so no leg records sizes and `crossedBudget` has nothing to compare. Capture **sizes for a\n96\tnamed method set**, not instruction listings: every use in this campaign was \"how big is this method\".\n97\tGuard on the classes matching the leg's sha, and record absence rather than guessing.\n98\t\n99\t### 8. Orphaned `Investigate.adjudicate`\n100\tThe report proposes experiments and cannot score them. This is the one genuine new shape (baseline,\n101\tisolation, target) and the only place I think a new entrypoint is justified.\n102\t\n103\t### 9. `allocConservation` must explain itself\n104\tCalled in `runLeg`, can fail a leg, and its result never reaches any output.\n105\t\n106\t### 10. `Ingest` records a warmup it cannot know\n107\t`Ingest.scala` writes `warmup = Bench.WarmupIterations` unconditionally. `e6-base-wi25` was measured at\n108\t`-wi 25` and is **stored as 10**.
