A command is another thing to remember, and forgetting is the\n113\t  problem being solved.\n114\t- **No new statistics.** The replicate statistic, the A/A null and the resolution floor are validated.\n115\t- **No claim the data cannot support**, specifically no row→method attribution from a whole-class leg.\n116\t\n117\t## Ordering\n118\t\n119\t1, 2, 4, 5, 6 first: all are wiring or correcting existing logic, none needs new capture, and each\n120\tcloses a case where the tool held the answer. Then 3 (the renderer), 9, 10. Then 7 (capture) and 8\n121\t(new entrypoint), which are the only two that add rather than connect.\n122\t"}]},"uuid":"7330b806-11e1-4888-a97f-0482787f7c7d","timestamp":"2026-08-17T16:03:56.378Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"09cd1a21-03ea-4d62-83e3-0c7be3b8b8f6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

{"parentUuid":"8db49598-f0ce-43f2-8228-98a3967516c6","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"139ba21f-1391-4d71-a553-c2fd88647ef0","agentId":"af5a83bcca1649bc3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EUJDLGcMyFxST3rfFfTcNA","type":"tool_result","content":"-rw-r--r--@ 1 fwbrasil  staff  6127 Aug 17 12:28 REVIEW-FINDINGS-PLAN.md\n---\n# Held-out review of the improvement plan: findings, and what I verified\n\nThe reviewer re-derived the replicated sweep's thresholds from the five stored legs independently and\nreproduced the tool's numbers exactly, so its arithmetic is checked against the harness rather than\nagainst my writeups. I then spot-checked its two highest-value claims myself. **Both hold.**\n\n## The thesis is wrong, and the wrong half is load-bearing\n\nMy plan claimed the tool \"refuses well and volunteers poorly\". Classifying all 29 defects by shape,\nthe reviewer found: **7** cases of the tool stating something wrong or silently substituting a weaker\nthing, **8** guards that did not guard, **6** missing capabilities, and only **3-4** genuine\nhad-the-data-did-not-say-it. So my diagnosis covers about one defect in eight.\n\nThe dominant failure is **a confident statement that was wrong, or was not the statement it claimed to\nbe**. Four of my five section-A items add a *new derived claim* to the report, landing squarely in the\ncategory that has produced seven wrong outputs, and the plan proposed no new cross-validation for any\nof them.\n\n## Two findings I verified myself\n\n**1. `bench compare` and `bench chain` never run the A/A null.** `Bench.nullComparison` and\n`Report.nullBlockers` have exactly two call sites in the harness, `Cli.scala:210` and `Cli.scala:215`,\nboth inside `BenchBracket`. So re-reading a stored bracket through `compare` reproduces the replicated\nverdict and **silently drops the strongest refusal the tool has** — the one `Bench.scala` calls \"the\nonly check here that can fail in the direction that matters\". This is defect 27 one level up, and it\nis not in my plan. `bench chain` never checks itself on any step.\n\n**2. `Bench.KnownNoise` is incomplete and the tool prints a wrong number because of it.**\nIt is `Seq(\"BoxesRunTime\", \"java.lang.Integer\", \"jmh_generated\")`. On the only real CPU profile in the\nrepository it matches `boxToInteger` at 29.1% and **nothing else**: the benchmark's own generated code\nis `ProtoKernelBench.loop$9` (17.1%), `run$39` (13.2%), `ask` (11.1%), `anon$95.<init>` (6.7%), none\nof which contain `jmh_generated`. So `noiseShare` reports **29%** where the true non-kernel share is\n**70%**, under the sentence \"% of sampled time is in classes no kernel change can move\" — understated\nby 41 points, biased toward making the kernel look more relevant than it is. Its test fixture cannot\ncatch this, being two authored frames with no `ProtoKernelBench` in them: **a live instance of open\ndefect 9.**\n\n## A factual error of mine that propagated\n\n`bench-results/sweep-replicated/RESULT.md` and `WORK.md` both say \"the two largest deltas do not\nresolve\", naming −12.5% and −10.7%. **The largest delta on the board is `trailingMapsStayLinear` at\n+43.2%, also flat.** It is three, not two. The plan inherited it from the writeup. This is the\ncounterintuitive fact the campaign leans on hardest and I stated it wrong in three documents.\n\n## The finding I would not have reached\n\nThe reviewer split each row's threshold into its two terms, `max(t·se, ownError·controlMean)`, and\nfound **7 of 15 rows are floor-bound**, i.e. their resolution is set by the legs' own JMH error rather\nthan by between-leg spread. Including this one:\n\n> **`handleLoopAnswersInPlace` is −10.7% against a ±14.4% resolution set entirely by the own-error\n> floor; its between-leg spread term is ±8.2%.** Halve the legs' own error and that row resolves as a\n> **win**.\n\nThat is the exact row whose demotion turned the sweep's \"five wins\" into three. So the campaign's most\nconsequential flat verdict sits on a threshold that forks would plausibly have moved, while\n`Plan.scala` tells the operator, unconditionally, that \"forks do not help\" — a claim resting on one\nA/A on one row, which on inspection cut own error ~2x (not six-fold) and made the spread term *worse*.\n\n**The item this yields, which beats everything in my plan:** annotate the existing `resolves` column\nwith which term binds. `±14.4% (own error)` is fixed by forks or longer iterations; `±12.6% (spread)`\nis fixed by more legs. Both terms are already computed inside `Stats.threshold`. Nothing needs\nmeasuring to say it.\n\n## Verdict per item\n\n**Cut:** A2 (not implementable: the four readings span different stores, and the runs that matter have\nno `jvmArgs`, so it would fire on differences the store cannot explain), A3 as written (no CPU profile\nexists in any campaign store except two QA fixtures, and `Run.cpu` has no row key, so it is a schema\nchange plus a re-measurement rather than a synthesis), B2 (contradicted by the tool's own text and by\nthe floor analysis above), C2 (busywork; covered by B1).\n\n**Keep with rework:** A1 (evidence wrong, three rows not two; make it a table property not appended\nprose), A4 (premise wrong: `budgetCandidates` has no CLI surface at all, so the item is *adding the\ncommand*, not labelling it), A5 (needs a stated selection rule; pooling a whole store mixes shas,\nconfigurations and sessions).\n\n**Keep as-is:** B3, C1.\n\n## Recommended order, which I accept\n\n1. Run the A/A null in `compare` and `chain` (missing refusal)\n2. Fix `KnownNoise`, name the top noise frames, fixture from the real capture\n3. Annotate `resolves` with its binding term (replaces A1's prose and B2 entirely)\n4. B3, dangling configuration reference\n5. Fix the `-f N is diagnostic` note to key on `df == 0` rather than fork count\n6. Give `budgetCandidates` a CLI surface, partitioned kernel/non-kernel\n7. B1, after (1)\n8. A5 with the selection rule\n9. C1\n10. A1 reduced to table ordering, acceptance corrected to three rows\n11. Fix `Ingest` warmup provenance: it writes `warmup = 10` unconditionally, so `e6-base-wi25`,\n    measured at `-wi 25`, is **stored as a falsehood**. Unfiled, and defect 25's family with the sign\n    flipped: not a missing field but a fabricated one.\n\n## Ledger drift the reviewer caught\n\n`WORK.md` still says \"Twenty-three tool defects... twenty-one fixed\" against the current 29/25, and\nstill states defect 9's open part as \"runs on request rather than every session\", which defect 24\nclosed.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"1f98c821-3a8c-4c49-933c-5163d80abc55","timestamp":"2026-08-17T16:03:57.666Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8db49598-f0ce-43f2-8228-98a3967516c6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

{"parentUuid":"60e289ed-11d4-49c3-b3a6-35447eafac88","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"139ba21f-1391-4d71-a553-c2fd88647ef0","agentId":"af5a83bcca1649bc3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DySueXUeEwP1SskBRc1GUk","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport Model.*\n2\timport kyo.*\n3\t\n4\t/** Parses HotSpot's `-XX:+LogCompilation` XML.\n5\t  *\n6\t  * This is the sole source of inlining decisions. `PrintInlining` reports a verdict and a byte count and nothing reliable beyond that: its\n7\t  * output interleaves across compiler threads, so its tree cannot be trusted. Here every decision sits beside the `<method>` element that\n8\t  * declares the callee's size, in structure, and the log additionally carries what that one cannot:\n9\t  *\n10\t  *   - deoptimizations that actually happened, which are invisible everywhere else\n11\t  *   - receiver counts per call site, so monomorphic against megamorphic is measured rather than asserted\n12\t  *   - OSR compilations, which is where a benchmark's loop body actually lives\n13\t  *\n14\t  * Ids are scoped to a compilation task and reused across tasks, so the symbol table is rebuilt per `<task>`.\n15\t  *\n16\t  * Three distinctions here were each responsible for a wrong conclusion, and are preserved deliberately:\n17\t  *\n18\t  *   1. A call site with no `receiver` attribute is *unprofiled*, not megamorphic.\n19\t  *   2. An `<uncommon_trap>` with `thread=` is an event; one with `bci=` is a guard the compiler planted.\n20\t  *   3. A method's inlining verdict is per site. On a site where it did not, the parser\n30\t    // would take the receiver count as the call count and then call the site monomorphic, since\n31\t    // `recvd == count` becomes trivially true.\n32\t    private val AttrCount  = \"\"\"(?<![\\w_])count='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n33\t    private val AttrRecv   = \"\"\"receiver='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n34\t    private val AttrRecvN  = \"\"\"receiver_count='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n35\t\n36\t    // by shape, for the same reason as the rest: fixing `id` before `name` is one reordering away\n37\t    // from silently dropping the symbol table\n38\t    private val Klass = \"\"\"<klass [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n39\t    // `bytes` and `iicount` are absent on the `unloaded='1'` form, so requiring both dropped 89 of 4466 declarations and left 118 call\n40\t    // sites resolving to raw ids downstream.\n41\t    private val Method     = \"\"\"<method [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n42\t    private val AttrId     = \"\"\"(?<![\\w_])id='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n43\t    private val AttrHolder = \"\"\"holder='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n44\t    /** The log is XML, so its attribute values are escaped, and a constructor arrives as `&lt;init&gt;`.\n45\t      *\n46\t      * Every other tool in this ladder prints `<init>`: javap, async-profiler, the JVM's own\n47\t      * `PrintInlining`. {"parentUuid":"12a60356-a76e-4af4-9764-56a4b35a8cf9","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"af5a83bcca1649bc3","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Ce8cMXWN6xJke3oWhYs4z","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Held-out review: `IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md` (v2)\n\nI verified the selector table by enumerating every `def` in the eleven production sources and counting references in production files versus test/QA files, then hand-checking every ambiguous case. I also attacked item 2 directly against a real 4 MB compilation log. Findings below, most consequential first.\n\n---\n\n## 1. The thesis: correct, and **understated by about a factor of two**. The table has two errors, both in the direction of flattering the tool\n\nThe organizing claim — result-driven selectors exist, are tested, and are on no code path — holds and is the right frame. But the count is wrong. Verified reference counts (production files: `Bench Store Stats Plan Investigate Bytecode LogCompilation Model Ingest Roots Cli`; the count includes the definition line itself, so `prod=1` means *zero callers*):\n\n**Two rows of your table are wrong, both claiming \"wired\" where nothing is:**\n\n- **`Bench.actionableJit` — you list it \"yes, 1 call\" (`:15`). It has zero callers and zero tests.** Repo-wide, `actionableJit` appears in exactly two places: its own definition at `Bench.scala:32`, and your plan's table. It is the only selector in the harness with *neither* a call site nor a test, and it carries a 6-line docstring (`Bench.scala:26-31`) documenting a reason vocabulary \"verified against a capture.\"\n\n- **`LogCompilation.diffVerdicts` — you list it \"yes, via `Comparison.jitChanges`\" (`:14`). It is transitively unwired.** Its only production reference besides the definition is `LogCompilation.scala:362`, inside `efficacy`, which your own table correctly marks unwired. `Comparison.jitChanges` is produced by `Bench.jitShift` (`Bench.scala:590`, `:757`), a *separate implementation* over `Run.jit` rather than over two `Parsed` logs. So this row is worse than unwired: it is **duplicated logic, one copy wired and one not**, in different modules over different types — the same defect Phase 7 already found once with `bracketPlan` (`WORK.md:385-389`).\n\nSo your eight rows are **one wired, seven not**, not three and five.\n\n**And the table misses at least six more unwired result-driven selectors:**\n\n| selector | production references | status |\n|---|---|---|\n| `Bench.allocConservation` | `Bench.scala:324` (def), `:331` (`end`) | **zero callers** |\n| `Bench.jitUnstable` | `Bench.scala:804` (def) | zero callers |\n| `Bench.measureDrift` | `Bench.scala:171` (def), `:185` (`end`) | zero callers |\n| `Stats.residual` | `Stats.scala:191` (def) | zero callers |\n| `Bytecode.verifyAgainst` | `Bytecode.scala:149` (def) | zero callers |\n| `ParseCoverage.show` / `Run.coverage` | captured `Bench.scala:507` | never rendered anywhere |\n\n**Item 9 is factually wrong.** You write \"`allocConservation` … Called in `runLeg`, can fail a leg\" (`:104`). It is not called in `runLeg` or anywhere else. What `runLeg` has at `Bench.scala:478-484` is a *different* guard — `evidence == Full && allocSites.nonEmpty && byMethod.isEmpty` — which checks the collapsed view is non-empty, not that it conserves. The actual conservation check, the one `WORK.md:169-171` credits with \"exact, 7,481 samples across 1,951 collapsed lines, nothing lost\" and with correctly refusing a two-recording pair, is a sixth unwired selector. Item 9 should be renumbered into the same class as items 1 and 5 (wire an unwired selector), not treated as a rendering omission.\n\n**One wired-but-dead case, which your framing predicts but does not list.** `Stats.commonMode` *is* called — `Bench.scala:729`, `val common = Stats.commonMode(reps)` — and `common` is referenced nowhere in the remaining 29 lines of `compareReplicated`. Its only possible consumer, `Stats.residual`, has zero callers. So every replicated comparison computes the session's common-mode drift and discards it. That is the category you asked me to hunt for and it exists.\n\n**`Run.coverage` deserves its own line.** `Model.scala:162-166` says carrying the parse fraction \"turns a silent partial parse into a visible one.\" It does not: `coverage` is stored on every Full leg and read by no renderer (`grep coverage Store.scala Cli.scala` → 0). `ParseCoverage.show`'s `(INCOMPLETE)` marker cannot be printed. A parser that reads 637 of 5093 elements still looks, from the operator's side, exactly like one that read all of them — which is the failure the field was added to prevent.\n\n**The one link I cannot verify** is the causal half: \"every throwaway probe written during this campaign called one of the five\" (`:26`). The probes are gone; I have no artifact for that. The *structural* claim is verified and is sufficient on its own — untestable logic on no code path is a defect regardless of what the probes did. I would state it structurally and drop the unverifiable causal sentence, because it is the one sentence in the finding that a reader could not check.\n\n**Verdict: keep the thesis, fix the table.** Corrected, it is stronger: 1 of 8 wired, plus 6 more unwired, plus 1 computed-and-discarded, plus 1 captured-and-never-rendered.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Item 2's central claim is **false as stated**, and I can show you the join\n\nYou asked me to try to break it. It breaks.\n\nThe compilation log names the benchmark row **on the `<task>` element**, in `bench-results/exp1/logc-new-default.xml`:\n\n```\n<task compile_id='1040' compile_kind='osr'\n  method='kyo.kernel.bench.jmh_generated.ProtoKernelBench_continuationBodiesFuse_jmhTest\n          continuationBodiesFuse_avgt_jmhStub (...)'\n```\n\nThe row name appears twice: in JMH's generated class (`ProtoKernelBench_<row>_jmhTest`) and in the stub method (`<row>_avgt_jmhStub`).\n\n**And the harness already parses and stores it.** `LogCompilation.scala:170` reads exactly that attribute (`AttrName2 = \"\"\"method='([^']+)'\"\"\"`) into `Task.method`, and `Task.inlines` (`:127`, `:92`) holds the inlining decisions made *while compiling that task* — i.e. the inline tree rooted at that row's stub. The row key is present in `Parsed` right now, on every Full leg.\n\n**One `flatMap` throws it away.** `LogCompilation.inlining` (`:270-285`) does `p.tasks.filter(_.level >= 4).flatMap(_.inlines)`, collapsing across tasks and discarding `Task.method`.
